Job Purpose

Learn where the world connects.

 Dubai, UAE | 6 months | Starting 11 January 2027

Based in Dubai, the Emirates Group is a global aviation and travel organisation, home to Emirates, one of the world’s largest international airlines, and dnata, a leading global air and travel services provider.

Together, our businesses connect people and economies across the world, supported by teams working across technology, finance, commercial, people, customer experience, operations and many other areas.

Elevate is our highly selective six-month internship programme for exceptional university students and recent graduates who have already demonstrated strong academic achievement and the potential to succeed in a demanding, international environment.

With a limited number of places available, Elevate is designed for those who want to challenge themselves, learn quickly and build on the experience they have already gained.

You’ll join one of our corporate teams in Dubai, work alongside experienced colleagues and contribute to real business priorities while continuing to develop your skills.

The experience

Elevate is more than an opportunity to observe a global business. We expect our interns to contribute, learn quickly and make the most of every opportunity during their six months with us.

You will:

  • Contribute to real projects and business priorities.
  • Apply your analytical and problem-solving skills to real business challenges.
  • Work with colleagues across different functions, cultures and areas of expertise.
  • Build your communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Learn through hands-on experience, feedback and dedicated development opportunities.
  • Receive structured mid-point and final performance reviews.
  • Join a small cohort of high-potential interns starting their journey together in Dubai.

Where could you join us?

Placements are available across Emirates and dnata in a range of corporate career areas:

  • Finance & Audit: financial planning and analysis, internal audit and financial projects.
  • Strategy, Data & Technology: strategy, business improvement, analytics, artificial intelligence and technology.
  • People, Legal & Risk: human resources, legal, privacy, safety and workplace wellbeing.
  • Commercial & Customer: commercial projects, loyalty, travel, cargo and customer experience.
  • Operations: service delivery, operational planning and performance.

Projects will vary by placement. You could find yourself analysing data to inform a business decision, researching a strategic opportunity, exploring how AI can improve the way we work, or contributing to improvements in an employee or customer experience.

When you apply, you’ll tell us which areas interest you most. We’ll consider your academic background, experience, skills and interests when matching shortlisted candidates to available placements.

Qualification

Do you have what it takes to Elevate?

Places on Elevate are limited and selection will be highly competitive. We are looking for candidates who have already distinguished themselves through their academic achievements, previous experience and the way they approach challenges.

To be eligible, you must:

  • Be in the final year of a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree, or have graduated less than a year ago.
  • Demonstrate a strong academic track record.
  • Have completed at least one previous internship, ideally within a multinational or international organisation.
  • Be available to work full-time in Dubai for six months.
  • Have not previously completed an internship with the Emirates Group.

Beyond meeting the eligibility criteria, successful candidates will need to demonstrate:

  • Strong analytical and structured problem-solving skills.
  • Learning agility and the ability to get up to speed quickly.
  • Initiative and ownership, with evidence of making things happen.
  • Clear and confident communication.
  • The ability to collaborate effectively with people from different backgrounds.
  • A track record of achievement, whether through your studies, previous internships, extracurricular activities or other experiences.

We welcome candidates from a wide range of academic disciplines, including business, finance, economics, data and technology, engineering, law, human resources, psychology, communications, marketing, hospitality, tourism, supply chain, healthcare management and safety.

Some placements require a specific academic background.

Your six months in Dubai

For six months, Dubai will become your home as well as your workplace.

You’ll experience life at the heart of the Emirates Group, build connections with people from around the world and develop your professional experience in one of the world’s most international cities.

For candidates relocating to Dubai, we provide support with accommodation, travel and visa arrangements so you can focus on making the most of the experience.

Ready to Elevate?

Elevate is designed for a small cohort, and meeting the eligibility criteria does not guarantee progression through the selection process.

Our selection process is rigorous and includes online assessments and interviews designed to understand not only what you have achieved so far, but how you think, learn and approach challenges.

If you have already built a strong foundation and are ready to challenge yourself further, we’d like to hear from you.

Apply now for the Elevate Internship Programme.

Salary & benefits

What we offer

Your Elevate package includes:

  • AED 5,000 monthly salary.
  • Accommodation: company-provided accommodation at Premier Inn Hotel, or an AED 2,000 monthly accommodation allowance.
  • Flights: travel to Dubai at the start of your internship and home at the end.
  • Visa & Emirates ID: fully sponsored.
  • Medical insurance.
  • Staff travel: one staff travel ticket upon successful completion of your internship.
  • Emirates Platinum membership: access to discounts across restaurants, retail, hotels and experiences in the UAE.

Social Media & Multimedia Production Intern, Planet Hub, BPPS (Home-based)

Job Identification: 36837
Posting Date: 09/11/2026
Apply Before: 09/25/2026
Job Schedule: Full time
Locations: Panama City, Panama
Agency: UNDP
Grade: IN
Vacancy Type: Internship Programme
Practice Area: Nature, Climate and Energy
Bureau: Bureau for Policy and Programme Support
Contract Duration: 6 months
Vacancy Timeline: 2 Weeks

Background

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion are core principles at UNDP:  we value diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate, we foster inclusion as a way of ensuring all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, and we ensure equity and fairness in all our actions. Taking a ‘leave no one behind’ approach to our diversity efforts means increasing representation of underserved populations. People who identify as belonging to marginalized or excluded populations are strongly encouraged to apply. Learn more about working at UNDP including our values and inspiring stories.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organisation for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realise the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP’s policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. In this context, UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan.

UNDP’s 2026–2029 Strategic Plan reaffirms our continued commitment to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals by accelerating structural transformations that advance poverty eradication, reduce inequalities, strengthen resilience, and drive sustainable, climate-aligned development.

Within the GPN, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) has the responsibility for developing all relevant policies and guidance to support the results of UNDP’s Strategic Plan. BPPS’s staff provides technical advice to Country Offices; advocates for UNDP corporate messages, represents UNDP at multi-stakeholder fora, including public-private dialogues, government, and civil society dialogues, and engages in UN inter-agency coordination in specific thematic areas.

As part of GPN in BPPS, UNDP’s Healthy Planet Hub promotes and scales up an integrated approach to deliver UNDP’s environment portfolio across nature, climate, energy, and chemicals and waste, supporting countries in advancing implementation of the Paris Agreement, the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, and related multilateral environmental agreements. It coordinates UNDP’s flagship offers—Nature Pledge, Climate Promise, and Energy Moonshot, and Cooling, Circularity and Pollution Prevention initiatives—to meet strong country demand across more than 140 countries. The Hub enables joined-up policy, programming, and financing solutions that accelerate low-emission, nature-positive, and pollution-free development, while strengthening resilience and advancing sustainable, inclusive growth in line with the Strategic Plan.

Food Systems are fundamental to the sustainable development of the 170 countries UNDP supports. Food Systems are often the largest contributor to their economies; food and nutrition are fundamental for citizen health; and Food Systems have a key role to play in achieving the SDGs. Yet, Food Systems are in crisis and need to be radically transformed to become sustainable. UNDP, building on its experience, has for the first time consolidated its Food Systems support and vision into this Strategy. The challenges and need for change related to Food Systems have been highlighted by a suite of reports by many research and international organizations and think tanks. The production practices and consumption patterns of food and agricultural commodities are taking these systems on an unsustainable trajectory with multiple impacts on human development, the environment, and economies; from ecosystem degradation, conflicts over land and natural resources, reduced capacity and resilience to climate and other shocks, persistent poverty, food insecurity and related people displacement and migration, to malnutrition including overweight and obesity. There is a clear need to work in a systemic and integrated manner to transform the Food Systems towards sustainability.

UNDP´s Vision for Food Systems 2030 is, through partnerships, to transform food and agricultural commodity systems into resilient; equitable; healthy, inclusive; environmentally, socially, and economically sustainable systems. Working on Food Systems will contribute to not only recovery from the COVID-19 crisis, by creating sustainable and resilient livelihoods for many along the Food Systems supply chains, but also to preventing further zoonoses from emerging in the future. This will require a change in the current paradigm of agricultural production focusing on maximizing productivity to a new paradigm based on diversified agroecological systems that work simultaneously on achieving economic, environmental, social, and health outcomes, with smallholders as a key part of the solution in their role as the engine of economic development. A Food Systems practice has been established within UNDP´s Nature, Climate, and Energy team, which is tasked to support UNDP Country Offices with Food Systems-
UNDP Nature Hub is the arrowhead of UNDP’s commitment to a “Nature Pledge” that aims to put nature at the heart of sustainable development. UNDP’s Nature Pledge for 2030 focuses on three systemic shift areas: value shift, economic and finance shift and policy and practice shift; that are necessary to trigger accelerated and scaled action for achievement of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF).

As part of the Planet Hub, the Food Systems team contribute to the Nature Pledge through the transformation of food and agricultural commodity systems into resilient, equitable, inclusive, environmentally, socially and economically sustainable systems. With a global portfolio invested in projects related to Food and Agricultural Commodity Systems and spread over 137 countries, UNDP seeks to promote a new paradigm for food and agricultural commodity systems that is based on diversified, resilient, agroecological systems and value chains which work simultaneously on achieving economic, environmental, social and health outcomes, with smallholders central to the transformation as the engine of economic development.

The Food Systems Team is seeking to recruit a Social Media & Multimedia Production Intern who will provide support in the development, coordination and implementation of communications and content production activities across ongoing initiatives, with a focus on social media and multimedia production.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Under the supervision of the Senior Knowledge Learning and Impact Advisor, the incumbent performs the following tasks:
  • Assisting in the creation of communications content for UNDP Food Systems social media channels (LinkedIn and YouTube).
  • Assisting in the design of visuals, social media cards, and infographics using Adobe Creative Suite (Illustrator, Premiere Rush/Pro); Canva and/or other relevant tool.
  • Editing and producing video content, including reels, recap videos, and event highlights, based on briefs and creative direction provided by the Communications Analyst.
  • Formatting and designing communications materials.
  • Assisting in the preparation of presentations, briefing notes, meeting minutes, and reports.
  • Supporting the execution of UNDP Food Systems campaigns and communications strategies across channels.
  • Providing support on internal communications reporting and products.
  • Other related tasks and ad hoc support.

Competencies

  • Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pay attention to details, deliver quality work by deadline
  • Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is a pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements
  • Learn Continuously:  LEVEL 1: Open-minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback
  • Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible
  • Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in the face of adversity, confident
  • Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships
  • Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

Candidates must meet one of the following criteria:
a)    Be enrolled in the final academic year of a first university degree programme (minimum bachelor’s level or equivalent) such as communications, journalism, marketing, international development, or a related field; or
b)    Be enrolled in a graduate school programme (second university degree or equivalent, or higher) such as communications, journalism, marketing, international development; or any other related fields.
c)    Have recently graduated with a university degree (as defined in (a) and (b) above) and, if selected, must start the internship within one year of graduation.

Experience:

  • Domain of MS Office package;
  • Excellent communication, writing and editing skills;
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to handle multiple tasks under tight deadlines;
  • Knowledge of LinkedIn and social media platforms;
  • Familiarity with Mailchimp or other newsletter platforms is an asset;
  • Experience in communications, content creation, or social media management;
  • Experience in video editing and multimedia production;
  • Experience with graphic design tools (Adobe Suite, Canva);
  • Experience with additional AI tools for creative production (Runway, Adobe Firefly, ElevenLabs, or similar) is an asset.

Language requirements:

  • Fluency in English is required.
  • Fluency in Spanish is an advantage

Internship Conditions:

Applicants should become familiar with the internship conditions prior to signing an internship agreement. For information visit www.undp.org/internships/

Institutional Arrangements

The intern will report to the Senior Knowledge Learning and Impact Advisor.

Financial aspects, expenses, and medical benefits

  • UNDP will not pay for the internship but may provide a monthly stipend in accordance with the provisions of the UNDP Internship policy.
  • UNDP accepts no responsibility for the medical insurance for the intern or for any costs arising from accidents and/or illness during the internship period. Interns, whether engaged in-person or remotely, are responsible for securing adequate medical insurance for the duration of their internship with UNDP and must provide self-certification of good health prior to starting the internship. UNDP will not reimburse the medical insurance of the intern. Any costs arising from accidents and illness incurred during an internship assignment will be the responsibility of the intern.
  • UNDP is not responsible for any claims by an intern or third party in the case of loss or damage to property or death or personal injury because of actions or omissions on the part of the intern during the internship period.

Working conditions:

  • When completing an in-person internship in a UNDP Office, interns must be provided with the workspace and equipment necessary to accomplish the activities related to the internship.
  • When completing a remote internship, interns will be responsible for providing their own equipment, internet and communication access, and workspace.

Subsequent Employment
There is no expectation of employment with UNDP following an internship.

Important note:

  • Interns are considered as gratis personnel. They are not staff members.
  • Interns may not be sought or accepted as substitutes for staff to be recruited against authorized posts.
  • Interns may not represent UNDP in any official capacity.

Application

Please provide the following documents to be considered:

  • CV
  • Motivational Letter

In case an applicant is successfully selected, s/he will be requested to provide electronic versions of:

  • Letter from his/her university confirming current enrolment and graduation date.
  • Copy of his/her most recent school transcript.
  • Copy of passport.
  • Completed UNDP internship application form.
  • Signed UNDP Internship Agreement.
  • Medical Certificate of Good Health.
  • Proof of medical insurance.

Kindly note the above documentation is required within one week after selection.
Disclaimer

Important information for US Permanent Residents (‘Green Card’ holders)

Under US immigration law, acceptance of a staff position with UNDP, an international organization, may have significant implications for US Permanent Residents. UNDP advises applicants for all professional level posts that they must relinquish their US Permanent Resident status and accept a G-4 visa, or have submitted a valid application for US citizenship prior to commencement of employment.

UNDP is not in a position to provide advice or assistance on applying for US citizenship and therefore applicants are advised to seek the advice of competent immigration lawyers regarding any applications.

Applicant information about UNDP rosters

Note: UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement.  We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Non-discrimination

UNDP has a zero-tolerance policy towards sexual exploitation and misconduct, sexual harassment, and abuse of authority. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks, and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles.

UNDP is an equal opportunity and inclusive employer that does not discriminate based on race, sex, gender identity, religion, nationality, ethnic origin, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, age, language, social origin or other status.

Scam warning

The United Nations does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process. Should you receive a solicitation for the payment of a fee, please disregard it. Furthermore, please note that emblems, logos, names and addresses are easily copied and reproduced. Therefore, you are advised to apply particular care when submitting personal information on the web.

content.rendered:
Information Technology Department: System Administrator – Cloud, Windows & Linux Infrastructure: Officer / Junior Officer (1)
Job Code: MLBL 083.84.03
Location: Head Office
Application Deadline: 7th October, 2026

Job Specification:

Highly skilled System Administrator to manage, secure, and optimize our IT infrastructure. The role requires solid experience in Windows and Linux server administration, virtualization, cloud platforms, networking, and security.

Key Responsibilities:

Server Administration (Windows & Linux):

  • Manage and troubleshoot Windows Server (2016/2019/2022) including Active Directory, DNS, DHCP, and GPOs.
  • Administer Linux servers (CentOS, RHEL, Ubuntu) and windows based systems.
  • Mount and manage enterprise server (e.g., DELL, IBM, LENEVO).
  • Mount and manage enterprise storage (e.g., DELL EMC NAS, RAID).
  • Automate system tasks using PowerShell, Bash, and Ansible.

Virtualization & Cloud Platforms:

  • Deploy and maintain infrastructure using VMware, KVM, Nutanix, Oracle Cloud, OpenStack.
  • Disaster recovery planning and cloud backups.
  • Research, deploy, and maintain IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS like platforms.

Network Administration (Preferred):

  • Configure and monitor Cisco, Fortinet, Huawei, and Palo Alto firewalls, routers, and switches.
  • Manage VPNs, NAT, BGP, and SD-WAN infrastructure.
  • Support both L2 and L3 network setups.

Containers & DevOps Tools:

  • Deploy and manage Docker, Podman, and Kubernetes environments.
  • Familiar with Open Shift, CI/CD pipelines, and version control using Git.

Security & Monitoring:

  • Perform server and network hardening (Windows/Linux).
  • Manage IPS/IDS (e.g SIEM), endpoint protection, and SSL.
  • Develop and manage monitoring scripts and alerts.
  • Manage and configure zabbix or equivalent monitoring system.

Minimum Required Experience:

3 to 5 years of hands-on experience in:

  • System administration (Windows and Linux)
  • Virtualization and container platforms
  • Network configuration and firewall management
  • Cloud-based infrastructure (AWS or equivalent)
  • Automation and monitoring tool

Minimum Required Certifications:

To be considered for this role, candidates must possess at least three of the following certifications:

  • Red Hat Certified System Administrator (RHCSA)
  • Microsoft Certified: Windows Server Administration Fundamentals (or equivalent)
  • Cisco Certified Network Associate (CCNA)
  • Google IT Support Professional Certificate
  • IBM or DELL or Linux Systems Certificate
  • Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) – Training Completed or In Progress
  • Ansible Automation Certification – Intermediate level
  • Virtualization Technology ( e.g VMware , Open shift etc)

Preferred Certifications:

  • Kubernetes CKA (Certified Kubernetes Administrator)
  • AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate
  • Linux Foundation LFCA or LFCS
  • Certified Ethical Hacking (CEH) – Trained or Certified
  • Cisco,Palo Alto or Sophos or fortinet Firewall Certification

Qualification:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Information Technology (BSc. CSIT, BCA, BIT, BE Computer, BIM, BSc. ICT) from a recognized university.

Age Critera:

Officer Level: Age not less than 21 years and not exceeding 40 years as of vacancy deadline.

title.rendered: Head – Compliance Department: Senior Manager / Manager / Deputy Manager

content.rendered:
Position: Head – Compliance Department: Senior Manager / Manager / Deputy Manager (1)
Job Code: MLBL 083.84.02
Location: Head Office
Application Deadline: 7th October, 2026

Job Purpose:

Head – Compliance is responsible for developing, implementing, and overseeing the Bank’s Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Counter Financing of Terrorism (CFT) programs. The role ensure compliance with local and international regulatory requirements, conduct risk assessments, and monitor suspicious transactions. The role involves reporting to regulatory bodies and advising senior management on compliance and financial crime risk.

Key Responsibilities

1. AML/CFT Strategy and Governance

  • Develop and implement an enterprise-wide AML/CFT compliance framework aligned with regulatory expectations and best practices.
  • Oversee the formulation of policies, procedures, and programs to detect, prevent, and report money laundering, terrorist financing, and other financial crimes.
  • Ensure continuous enhancement of risk-based AML/CFT approaches across all business lines and geographies.

2. Regulatory Compliance Management

  • Ensure full compliance with all applicable laws, directives, circulars, and guidelines issued by regulators such as NRB, FIU, and international bodies (FATF, Basel, etc.).
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for regulatory bodies on AML/CFT and compliance matters.
  • Prepare and submit accurate and timely regulatory reports, including STRs and CTRs, to the FIU.

3. Transaction Monitoring & Investigation

  • Supervise the deployment and optimization of automated transaction monitoring systems.
  • Lead case reviews, investigations, and the decision-making process on STRs and potential breaches.
  • Oversee customer due diligence (CDD), enhanced due diligence (EDD), and ongoing monitoring of high-risk accounts.

4. Policy Development & Risk Assessment

  • Lead enterprise-wide compliance risk assessments, including AML/CFT, KYC, sanctions, and PEP exposure.
  • Design and update internal compliance policies and manuals in line with evolving regulatory expectations and risk assessments.
  • Guide business units in embedding AML/CFT controls in product design and customer onboarding processes.

5. Training, Culture & Awareness

  • Build a strong compliance culture through regular training, communication, and awareness programs across all staff levels.
  • Ensure senior management and board awareness of key AML/CFT risks and compliance obligations.
  • Cultivate an ethical, zero-tolerance approach to non-compliance.

6. Internal Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement

  • Collaborate with business, risk, internal audit, IT, and legal departments to ensure effective enterprise-wide compliance.
  • Advise senior management and board committees on critical compliance risks and emerging threats.
  • Coordinate with law enforcement, FIU, and peer institutions for knowledge sharing and best practices.

Key Competencies

  • Regulatory Expertise: In-depth understanding of AML/CFT regulations, FATF standards, and Nepalese financial laws.
  • Analytical Thinking: Ability to assess complex data for potential money laundering risks and develop strategic responses.
  • Leadership: Skilled at leading multidisciplinary compliance teams and fostering a culture of integrity.
  • Technology Proficiency: Experience in compliance system implementation and data analytics for financial crime detection.
  • Communication: Strong written and verbal communication for engaging with regulators, senior management, and staff.
  • Risk Awareness: Sound knowledge of compliance risk management frameworks and methodologies.
  • Discretion & Integrity: High ethical standards and confidentiality in handling sensitive compliance matters.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • % of high-risk customer reviews completed on time
  • Number of STRs/CTRs filed and acted upon timely
  • Reduction in regulatory breaches and penalties
  • Average resolution time for alerts/investigations
  • Staff compliance training coverage and pass rate
  • Regulatory inspection outcomes (e.g., zero major findings)
  • System coverage of automated transaction monitoring
  • Effectiveness of KYC/CDD/EDD compliance rate

Qualification:

  • CA / Masters’ degree in Management or equivalent from the recognized university with second division or above.

Experience:

  • For Senior Manager Position: Minimum 10 years of experience in Commercial or National Level Development Banks with at least 6 years of experience in related job functions.
  • For Manager Position: Minimum 8 years of experience in Commercial or National Level Development Banks with at least 5 years of experience in related job functions.
  • For Deputy Manager: Minimum 7 years of experience in Commercial or National Level Development Banks with at least 4 years of experience in related job functions.
  • Candidates must have a minimum of 2 years of experience in their most recent position, and the last-held position must be at least at the level of Senior Officer in a Commercial Bank or Assistant Manager in a National Level Development Bank.

Age Criteria: Age not less than 25 years as of vacancy deadline.

title.rendered: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support Coordinator

content.rendered:
The Terre des hommes Foundation (Tdh), with headquarters in Lausanne and an office in Zurich, is the leading Swiss child rights organisation with more than 2000 employees worldwide. We stand together with children to uphold their rights, protect their lives and improve their well-being. We achieve this through innovative programmes focused on health, migration and access to justice, specially designed to have a positive and sustainable impact. For more detailed information, please visit our website at: Terre des hommes

Founded in 1960 and active in Nepal since 1985, Tdh has implemented impactful interventions in Maternal and Child Health, Migration, and WASH in Institutions, with a strong focus on Child Protection. All initiatives are carried out in close collaboration with government bodies and civil society organizations to ensure sustainable and child-centered outcomes.

Position: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) Coordinator

Report to: Child Protection (CP) and Migration Program Manager

Location: 30% Kathmandu 70% Field

Duration: 6 months with possiblity of extension

Application deadline: 30th September 2026

Background:

In response to the recent floods affecting Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading, Terre des hommes (Tdh) is implementing Safe Project through local implementing partner to support flood-affected children, families and communities. The project focuses on strengthening protection and resilience through integrated interventions in Child Protection in Emergencies (CPiE), Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA), and WASH.

The project will be implemented over an initial period of six months, with the possibility of extension based on needs, funding and project requirements.

Overview

Under direct supervision of Child Protection and Migration Program Manager, MHPSS Coordinator will provide technical leadership and support for planning, implementation, quality assurance and monitoring of MHPSS interventions under Safe project. The position will work closely with the implementing partner, relevant government authorities, Protection and MHPSS stakeholders and other project team members to ensure that MHPSS services are delivered in line with relevant standards, principles and good practices.

MHPSS Coordinator will also provide technical guidance and capacity-building support to implementing partner staff and contribute to strengthening safe, inclusive and context-appropriate psychosocial support mechanisms for children, caregivers and affected communities.

MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES

a) Technical Support

  • Provide technical support in planning and rollout of MHPSS models (e.g., PM+, SH+, STAND-UP, EASE etc.) and structured play and recreational activities.
  • Coordinate with and provide guidance to MHPSS Focal Person at local implementing partner ensuring quality delivery of project activities
  • Facilitate training on MHPSS models to build capacity of partner staff and mentor partner staff to ensure their quality delivery.
  • Ensure proper documentation, analysis, and reporting of MHPSS activities in line with Tdh’s data protection and confidentiality standards.
  • Develop necessary MHPSS related process guideline and checklists in support of MEAL and other team at Country Delegation/Regional/HQ.
  • Ensure MHPSS interventions comply with global and Tdh’s MHPSS and child protection standards and principles.
  • Identify and address gaps in MHPSS knowledge and skills among frontline Facilitator.

b) Project Management:

  • Support CP & Migration Program Manager in project management through developing project plan, implmentation through local partner and monitoring of project activities.
  • Conduct regular supervision and coaching sessions for facilitators and front-line workers delivering MHPSS services and document them.
  • Organize regular meetings with partner and report project progress.
  • Regularly update PFU in support of MEAL and SITREP.
  • Support in developing procurement plan of Safe Project, prepare weekly/monthly work plans, and contribute to the preparation of cash forecasts and logistics requests related to MHPSS.
  • Support in developing project reports in designed templates.
  • Report risks or challenges with suggested mitigation strategies

c) Coordination, advocacy and Networking:

  • Support in service mapping for MHPSS services and maintain relationships with service providers (specialized and non-specialized).
  • Facilitate partner in linking referrals for specialized and non-specialized MHPSS services in coordination with internal and external actors.
  • Coordination with internal and external stakeholders to ensure integrated programming.
  • Liaise with partners, CBOs, and relevant authorities to promote access to MHPSS services and support referrals and case discussions.

Qualifications & Experience:

  • Master’s Degree in Psychology, Social Science, Law or any other relevant subjects
  • At least 3 years’ experience in implementing CP program, experience of working in emergency context will be given preference.
  • Knowledge and experience of applying MHPSS Models
  • Have experience of facilitating trainings, managing project and partner.

Swisscontact, established in 1959 in Switzerland, is a leading partner organisation for the implementation of international development projects. The organisation promotes inclusive economic, social, and ecological development to make an effective contribution towards sustainable and widespread prosperity in developing and emerging economies. It strengthens the competencies of people, improving their employability, increases the competitiveness of enterprises, growing their business, and fosters social and economic systems, promoting inclusive development.

Swisscontact, registered as an International Non-Governmental Organisation in Nepal, has been operating in Nepal since 1991. Currently, Swisscontact in Nepal has six development programmes across all seven provinces.

The Municipal Revenue Enhancement Project (MunRev) is a bilateral initiative of the Governments of Nepal and Switzerland, implemented by the Ministry of Land Management, Cooperatives, Federal Affairs and General Administration (MoLMCFAGA) and selected 12 partner municipalities of Koshi and Bagmati Provinces, with technical assistance from Swisscontact in Nepal. MunRev supports local governments to strengthen own-source revenue and tax compliance, improve inclusive and transparent public service delivery, and foster cross-government learning for better-informed fiscal policy, with gender equality and social inclusion (GESI) mainstreamed throughout. Through these efforts, the project aims to enhance the fiscal capacity of local governments and improve services for all citizens, including women and disadvantaged groups.

Location: Biratnagar, Project Support Unit (PSU), with frequent travel to the 12 partner municipalities in Koshi and Bagmati Provinces
Reports to: Governance & Service Delivery (GSD) Advisor
Time: 100% (8 hours a day and 5 days a week)

Duration: One year initially, with the possibility of an extension

Purpose of the Job

The IT & Digitalization Officer will support the implementation, operation, and institutionalisation of digital systems for municipal revenue administration and service delivery. The position will strengthen municipal digital capacity, improve data quality and system integration, and provide technical support to partner municipalities to ensure effective and sustainable use of digital solutions.

Essential Functions and Responsibilities

1.Compliance with policies, rules/regulations, and guidelines

Adhere to relevant policies, procedures, rules, regulations, and guidelines of Swisscontact in Nepal (Country Manual for Business Administration, Code of Conduct Against Corruption, Conflict of Interest, Basic Operating Guideline (BoG), Local Security Management Plan, Gender Equality and Social Inclusion Guideline and other specific policies guidelines and manuals applicable for the MunRev).

2. Revenue Management Systems and Digitalization

  •  Support the implementation, enhancement, integration, and maintenance of municipal revenue management systems, including interoperability with national platforms such as SUTRA and LMBIS.
  •  Assist municipalities in digitizing revenue records, migrating and managing data, and improving the efficiency, quality, and utilization of digital revenue administration systems.

3. Municipal System Support and Technical Assistance

  •  Serve as the primary technical focal point for municipalities and coordinate with system vendors and relevant stakeholders.
  • Provide regular technical support, troubleshooting, and field-based assistance to ensure effective operation and maintenance of digital systems.
  • Maintain issue tracking, support municipalities during critical revenue operations, and recommend system improvements through periodic reporting.

4. Digitalization of Municipal Service Delivery

  • Support municipalities in digitalizing service delivery processes, including citizen services, permits, digital payments, and document management.
  •  Promote digital governance solutions that improve transparency, efficiency, accountability, citizen engagement, and access to public information.

5. Data Management, Integration and Analytics

  •  Support data management, quality assurance, integration, and security to ensure reliable and disaggregated information for municipal decision-making and project reporting.
  • Develop and maintain dashboards, reports, and analytical tools, and support data migration, validation, and utilization for learning and policy improvement. 6. ICT Infrastructure, Cybersecurity and System Administration
  •  Support the management and maintenance of ICT infrastructure, databases, networks, cloud applications, and backup systems in partner municipalities.
  •  Promote cybersecurity, data protection, system reliability, and user access management to ensure secure and uninterrupted operation of digital systems.

7. Capacity Development and Change Management

  • Design and deliver training, coaching, and technical support to strengthen municipal staff capacity in operating and managing digital systems.
  • Develop user manuals, SOPs, and guidance materials, and support municipal ownership, sustainability, and handover of project-supported digital solutions.

8. Project Coordination and Reporting

  •  Support project planning, monitoring, reporting, and procurement of ICT-related goods and services.
  • Coordinate with government agencies, development partners, and municipalities; document lessons learned and good practices; and perform other duties assigned by the GSD Advisor and the Team Leader

9. Key Deliverables

  •  Digitalization assessments and roadmaps developed for partner municipalities.
  • Functional and interoperable OSR MIS with improved data quality and reporting.
  • Technical support, system monitoring, and issue-resolution mechanisms established and maintained.
  •  Training delivered, and user manuals, SOPs, and guidance materials developed.
  • Dashboards, analytical reports, and sustainability plans produced to support effective use and longterm ownership of digital systems.

Qualifications and Competencies

  •  Bachelor’s degree in information technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related field.
  • Master’s degree in a relevant field will be an advantage.
  •  Minimum three years of relevant professional experience in IT systems management, MIS, digitalization, e-governance, or digital transformation initiatives.
  •  Experience working with local governments, public financial management systems, or development projects in Nepal is highly desirable.
  •  Practical knowledge of government systems such as SuTRA, LMBIS, LLRP, or other municipal information systems will be an advantage.
  •  Strong knowledge of database management, ICT infrastructure, systems integration, data analytics, cybersecurity, and digital governance applications.
  • Demonstrated analytical, problem-solving, communication, training, and stakeholder coordination skills, with the ability to support both technical and non-technical users.
  •  Excellent written and spoken Nepali and English, commitment to inclusive digital solutions, and willingness to travel extensively to partner municipalities.

Duty Station: NSET Office, Kathmandu, with field visits as required

1. Background
National Society for Earthquake Technology – Nepal (NSET) is nonprofit non-governmental organization working for Mult hazard risk management sector. It implements and supports various programs and projects related to disaster risk reduction, earthquake safety, resilient construction, humanitarian response, community resilience, and other related areas.

NSET requires dedicated support for monitoring, evaluation, accountability, learning, documentation, reporting, and communication across its different projects and programs. The MEAL Officer will provide organization-wide MEAL support and will be assigned to different projects and activities according to NSET’s requirements.

2. Purpose of the Position
The MEAL Officer will support NSET in strengthening its Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) systems across projects and programs. The position will also support project documentation, reporting, communication, and graphic/design-related requirements as assigned.

3. Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and implement MEAL/monitoring plans, log frames, indicators, assessment tools, trackers, and reporting formats in line with project requirements.
  • Monitor project progress, targets, activities, quality, outputs, outcomes, and timelines through regular follow-up and field visits.
  • Verify project activities, results, beneficiary information, and supporting documentation to ensure data quality and compliance.
  • Familiarity with data collection and management tools such as KoboToolbox, ODK, Google Forms, Excel, and other digital platforms.
  • Support baseline, endline, PDM, needs assessments, evaluations, and other project assessments.
  • Collect, compile, analyze, and present quantitative and qualitative data and provide evidence-based findings for project decision-making.
  • Establish and manage beneficiary feedback and complaint-response mechanisms.
  • Record, monitor, and follow up on feedback and complaints to strengthen accountability and responsiveness.
  • Promote accountability, safeguarding, confidentiality, inclusion, and appropriate MEAL standards across projects.
  • Document lessons learned, good practices, challenges, outcomes, and success stories.
  • Support project review, reflection, learning, and coordination meetings and follow up on agreed actions.
  • Prepare case studies, learning materials, reports, and other project documentation.
  • Prepare tables, charts, dashboards, presentations, and progress summaries for project monitoring and reporting.
  • Support project, organizational, and donor reporting by providing accurate, timely, and verified information.
  • Maintain organized MEAL records, databases, evidence, monitoring documents, and digital archives.
  • Prepare posters, brochures, factsheets, presentations, infographics, reports, banners, and social media materials using Canva and other appropriate design tools.
  • Provide MEAL, documentation, communication, and visibility support to NSET projects as assigned.

  • Experience with NGO/INGO or development projects is preferred.
  • Good knowledge of MS Office.
  • Experience in data visualization and reporting is preferred.
  • Knowledge of graphic design tools such as Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop, or equivalent is an advantage.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English and Nepali.
  • Willingness and ability to travel to project locations.

  • Data management and reporting skills
  • Good documentation and communication skills
  • Graphic/design skills
  • Attention to detail
  • Ability to work with multiple project teams
  • Good interpersonal and coordination skills

Position: Finance Assistant (Consultant) – Nepal Emergency Response

Location: Nepal

Project HOPE is an international NGO with more than 1,000 engaged employees and volunteers who work around the globe, responding to the world’s most pressing global health challenges. Throughout our 60-year legacy, Project HOPE has treated millions of patients, provided more than $3 billion worth of medicines to local health care organizations around the world helped build hundreds of health programs from the ground up, and responded to humanitarian crises worldwide.

Code of Conduct

It is our shared responsibility and obligation to treat each other with respect, take affirmative steps to prevent matters involving Sexual Exploitation & Abuse and Trafficking in Persons, and to disclose all potential and actual violations of our Code of Conduct, which may include Conflicts of Interest, Fraud, Corruption, Discrimination or Harassment. Together we can reinforce a culture of respect, integrity, accountability, and transparency.

Summary:

Project HOPE is seeking a Finance Assistant Consultant to provide administrative and financial support to its emergency response activities in Nepal. The consultant will support financial operations, including financial documentation, payment processing, petty cash tracking, transaction recording, reconciliations, and financial reporting while ensuring compliance with Project HOPE procedures, donor requirements, and applicable Nepal statutory requirements in a humanitarian operating environment.

In carrying out the scope of work, the consultant will coordinate, as needed, with the Finance Officer, relevant Project HOPE teams, vendors, and other stakeholders.

Purpose:

The purpose of this consultancy is to provide additional finance capacity to support Project HOPE’s Nepal emergency response and facilitate timely, accurate, and well-documented financial operations during the consultant assignment period.

Scope of Consultancy

The consultant will provide services in the following areas:

Financial Operations

  • Support recording and maintenance of financial transactions in the accounting system.
  • Review financial documentation for completeness, accuracy, and appropriate approvals.
  • Support payment processing, including vendor and consultant payments, advances, and other approved payments.
  • Prepare payment requests, advance clearances, and related supporting documentation.
  • Support month-end financial close activities and account reconciliations.

Cash and Financial Records

  • Support petty cash administration, documentation, tracking, and reconciliation.
  • Maintain payment, advance, contract, and other finance tracking records.
  • Ensure financial documents are properly organized, scanned, filed and archived.
  • Support preparation of weekly cash reports and monthly cash requests.

Compliance and Reporting

  • Review supporting documentation for procurement, travel, advances, and expenses to ensure compliance with Project HOPE and donor requirements.
  • Support preparation and processing of personnel-related payments, as applicable and as directed by the Finance Officer.
  • Assist with internal and donor financial reporting.
  • Support finance documentation and processes required under applicable Nepal laws and requirements, as directed.

Coordination

  • Coordinate with the Finance Officer, Nepal program and operations teams, vendors, implementing partners, and Project HOPE HQ Finance as appropriate.
  • Provide regular updates on finance activities, outstanding items, and issues requiring follow-up.

EXPECTED OUTPUTS

During the consultancy period, the consultant is expected to contribute to:

  • Timely and accurate recording of financial transactions.
  • Complete and properly maintained financial documentation and records.
  • Timely processing and tracking of payments, advances, and other approved financial obligations.
  • Accurate petty cash and cash management records and reconciliations.
  • Timely completion of monthly financial close activities and related reporting support.
  • Regular coordination and follow-up with Nepal and HQ Finance teams.
  • Detailed deliverables, timelines, and expectations will be outlined in the consultancy Statement of Work.

Duration of Assignment: Approximately 3-6 months

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Diploma or Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or related field.
  • Minimum 1–3 years of relevant experience in finance or administrative support, preferably in NGO, INGO, or humanitarian settings in Nepal.
  • Basic understanding of accounting, financial documentation, payment processing, and petty cash management.
  • Familiarity with applicable Nepal finance, tax, and statutory documentation requirements is preferred.
  • Experience supporting procurement documentation, vendor payments, cash advances, and reconciliations is desirable.
  • Strong attention to detail and demonstrated ability to maintain accurate financial documentation and records.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities, and meet deadlines in an emergency response environment.
  • Strong communication and coordination skills, including the ability to work effectively with field teams, vendors, financial institutions, and implementing partners.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Word and familiarity with electronic financial or accounting systems; NetSuite experience is desirable.
  • Fluency in Nepali and working proficiency in English are required.
  • The consultancy fee will be determined based on the scope of services, qualifications, and experience of the selected consultant.

Notice to applicants: Project HOPE does not conduct direct solicitation/recruitment via email. Project HOPE never asks consultant applicants for payment or financial information at any stage of the recruitment process. Project HOPE will never send you a third-party check and ask you to cash it. If you have been recruited via email, please contact Compliance@projecthope.org

Due to the substantial number of inquiries we receive, only those who meet the required qualifications and experience for this consultancy will be contacted. No phone calls please. However, since we are active around the world in the field of public health, we may wish to retain your CV in our database for other/future opportunities, unless you direct us otherwise.

Thank you very much for your interest in Project HOPE.

Position: Health and Nutrition Coordinator
Location: Kathmandu, Nepal

End Date: September 30, 2026

With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 31,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

Employee Contract Type: Local – Fixed Term Employee (Fixed Term)

Job Description:

World Vision International Nepal (WVI Nepal) has launched a Category II Emergency Response in the districts of Rasuwa and Nuwakot, Bagmati Province, following devastating flash floods along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river corridors that caused casualties, displacement and extensive damage across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading. The 12-month Nepal Flash Flood Response (NFFR) 2026 plan which is funded by several donors targets 25,000 people, including 10,000 children, from around 5,000 affected households across seven sectors, moving from relief into early recovery. This position will also support health and nutrition activities in the other emergency response project funded by the US government (RISE project) focuses on moderate acute malnutrition in districts of Madhesh Province (Mahottari, Sarlahi and Rautahat).

This position has responsibility to lead the health and nutrition activities in the Nepal Flash Flood Response project and RISE project to respond to emergency needs and to functionalize health, nutrition and hygiene (WASH) interventions. The activities will take place in the emergency response locations (Rasuwa and Nuwakot) and in WVI Nepal’s development program areas (such as in Mahottari, Sarlahi and Rautahat districts). The role ensures technically sound programming of World Vision and partner NGOs in the areas of health, nutrition and the hygiene component of WASH. The role will also ensure the technical aspects are compliant with WVI Nepal’s standards, government policies, and humanitarian norms. Key Responsibilities include:

Monitoring partner NGOs’ health, nutrition and hygiene program quality and project delivery.
Providing technical and functional support for quality health, nutrition and hygiene programming.
Leading on emergency nutrition actions including IYCF-E, screening, management of MAM and referral of SAM cases, community mobilization, and integrated health and WASH interventions.
Coordinating with government authorities, UN agencies, INGOs, and cluster coordination mechanisms
Developing annual technical support plans and rolling out tools, benchmarks, and guidance for emergency contexts and in development contexts, where relevant.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

Technical support in project implementation

  • Support the project and PNGO managers to implement health, nutrition and hygiene (related to WASH programming) planning, budgeting, implementation, monitoring, and support reporting to ensure achievement of agreed emergency response and DHR funded RISE project objectives, targets, and quality standards.
  • Provide overall technical leadership to the World Vision team and partner NGOs implementing nutrition interventions, including Positive Deviance (PD) Hearth,
  • Management of Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) and referral support for severe acute malnutrition, maternal health and nutrition, and integrated WASH activities.
  • Ensure timely and quality implementation of emergency nutrition interventions, including community screening, identification and referral of SAM and MAM cases, growth monitoring, child vaccination support, and hygiene interventions.
  • Conduct community awareness sessions on personal, household, and environmental hygiene. Educate community members on proper handwashing with soap at critical times, including before eating and after using the toilet.
  • Promote safe water handling, treatment, storage, and consumption practices to prevent waterborne diseases.
  • Capacity development of health operations and management committees to functionalize health systems at local health facility level.
  • Conduct regular program reviews with partners to assess progress, address bottlenecks, and strengthen implementation quality.
  • Lead project start-up, transition, close-out, and sustainability planning processes together with partners.
  • Facilitate integration of Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) principles throughout project planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation.

Emergency Preparedness and Response

  • Provide technical leadership and coordination for emergency health and nutrition responses, including floods, earthquakes, disease outbreaks, and other humanitarian emergencies.
  • Lead rapid needs assessments for health and nutrition and support emergency response planning, implementation, monitoring, and reporting.
  • Ensure implementation of emergency nutrition interventions, including IYCF-E, acute malnutrition screening and referral, micronutrient support, and hygiene activities.
  • Support emergency health response activities, including disease surveillance, rapid health assessments, referral of vulnerable cases, and coordination with health facilities to ensure timely access to essential health services.
  • Conduct community outreach and health awareness sessions on disease prevention, hygiene promotion, safe water practices, outbreak preparedness, and emergency health measures during disasters and public health emergencies.
  • Coordinate with government and humanitarian partners on emergency health, nutrition, vaccination, WASH, and health and nutrition related risk communication and community engagement activities.
  • Monitor public health and nutrition risks and support preparedness and response measures during emergencies.
  • Ensure integration of nutrition, health, WASH, with other sectors such as protection, and integrate psychosocial considerations within emergency responses.

Information Management and Learning

  • Ensure accurate, timely, and real-time collection, analysis, and reporting of nutrition-related data, including SAM/MAM caseloads, maternal nutrition indicators, and maternal, newborn, child health and nutrition service coverage.
  • Health and hygiene information management – timely information sharing on possible disease outbreaks and prepared mitigation measures as per the context.
  • Support the design and implementation of digital and paper-based monitoring systems that improve data quality and decision-making.
  • Collaborate closely with the MEAL team to roll out emergency information management systems such as SORMAS, 5Ws reporting, and other donor-required reporting mechanisms.
  • Conduct routine data verification, validation, and quality assurance exercises to ensure accuracy and reliability of program information.
  • Generate periodic analytical reports highlighting program achievements, gaps, trends, and recommendations for management decision-making.
  • Document and disseminate case studies, success stories, lessons learned, and best practices from both non-emergency health, nutrition and hygiene programming and emergency flood response interventions
  • Support the project managers to maintain proper program documentation and information management systems in compliance with organizational policies.

Capacity Strengthening and Technical Support

  • Assess technical and operational capacity gaps related to health, nutrition and hygiene related to WASH among partner staff and develop capacity-strengthening plans.
  • Provide technical guidance, coaching, mentoring, and supportive supervision to WVI Nepal staff, partners staff and government staff to improve program quality and effectiveness.
  • Strengthen partner capacity on key nutrition interventions, including:
  • Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) and IYCF in Emergencies (IYCF-E) practices (e.g. Exclusive breastfeeding promotion and support, complementary feeding for children aged 6-23 months).
  • Community-based management and referral of acute malnutrition.
  • Maternal nutrition interventions.
  • Super Cereal distribution and monitoring.
  • Support establishment and quality functioning of IYCF corners in shelters, temporary settlements, health facilities, and communities.
  • Strengthening community mobilization, behaviour change communication, and nutrition awareness initiatives in communities and schools.
  • Strengthening partner capacity on key health and hygiene interventions, including:
  • Community-based disease surveillance and outbreak preparedness and response.
  • Hygiene promotion, handwashing practices, and risk communication and community engagement.
  • Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) measures in community and health facility settings.
  • Maternal, newborn, and child health (MNCH) awareness and referral mechanisms.
  • Promote integration of GESI, disability inclusion, safeguarding, protection, and environmental sustainability across partner program.

Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning

  • Conduct regular field monitoring visits to assess programme quality, effectiveness, compliance, and beneficiary satisfaction.
  • Monitor project performance against approved indicators, benchmarks, work plans, and donor commitments.
  • Verify program data through spot checks, field observations, and review of partner reporting systems.
  • Work closely with the MEAL team to strengthen community feedback and accountability mechanisms and ensure appropriate response to beneficiary concerns.
  • Monitor coverage and quality of nutrition, health, and WASH services at community and facility levels.
  • Support evaluations, assessments, operational research, surveys, and learning reviews to enhance programme effectiveness.
  • Promote utilization of monitoring and learning findings for adaptive program management.

Risk Management & Compliance

  • Identify, assess, and monitor program risks related to public health emergencies, disease outbreaks, operational challenges, supply chains, and service delivery.
  • Develop and implement risk mitigation and contingency plans related to health, nutrition and hygiene programming in collaboration with partner NGOs, local authorities, and relevant stakeholders.
  • Ensure compliance with World Vision International policies, donor regulations, government guidelines, and humanitarian principles through engagement with partner NGOs and project visits.
  • Support partners in maintaining adequate documentation and evidence required for audits, donor reviews, and compliance assessments.
  • Strengthen accountability, transparency, safeguarding, and ethical practices throughout program implementation.

External Engagement and Coordination

  • Build and maintain productive relationships with provincial and local governments, UN agencies, INGOs, NGOs, and other stakeholders.
  • Represent World Vision International Nepal in nutrition, health, WASH, and emergency coordination forums at local and provincial levels.
  • Participate in relevant technical working groups, clusters, task forces, and coordination mechanisms.
  • Advocate for improved access to quality nutrition and health services for vulnerable populations.
  • Strengthening collaboration, information sharing, and joint planning among partners to enhance program effectiveness and avoid duplication.
  • Contributes to increased visibility, communication efforts and donor engagement by showcasing program achievements, impact, and learning.

KNOWLEDGE/QUALIFICATIONS FOR THE ROLE

Required Professional Experience

  • A 2-3 years proven record of health and nutrition experience working both in emergency and in development program

Required Education, training, license, registration and certification

  • Bachelor’s degree in Public Health, Nutrition, Nursing, or in the fields suitable for development.

Essential Knowledge and Qualifications

  • Knowledge of development and humanitarian industry.
  • Writing quality reports.
  • Data management.
  • Demonstrate collaboration & team building skills.
  • Effective relationship management skills; ability to influence without having authority.
  • Strong oral and written English and Nepali communication skills.
  • Ability to structure and manage one’s own work.

Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications

  • Cross-functional management experience in an I/NGO, UN/ bilateral organizational environment
  • Knowledge and experience of humanitarian response action in Nepal
  • Perform other organizational and business processes that are required to contribute to WVIN’s strategic objectives and to maintain a healthy organizational life
  • Demonstrate understanding of and commitment to World Vision’s Core Values in the approach to work and relationships
  • Ensure implementation of Child Protection Policy and Child Safe Organization practices

Work Base: Nuwakot District

Duration: One year

Travel and/or Work Environment

Field travel to flood-affected areas may be required. Field travel may involve difficult road conditions, disrupted access, remote locations and basic accommodation.

WVI Nepal has zero tolerance to child rights’ violations, by employees and/or affiliates.”
