NATIONAL POST: District Project Coordinator, Achham, Nepal, LSC-7
Job Identification: 36872
Apply Before: 09/29/2026, 11:59 PM
Job Schedule: Full time
Location: Nepal
Grade: LSC-7
Vacancy Type: Local Service Contract

Job Description

The Position:

The District Project Coordinator is a field-based project coordination position responsible for facilitating implementation of UNFPA-supported integrated sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) and gender-based violence (GBV) interventions across assigned districts and programme municipalities. The incumbent will maintain regular engagement with provincial, district and local authorities; coordinate implementing partners and service-delivery actors; monitor programme quality and results; and support timely follow-up and reporting.

The position connects municipal implementation with provincial and national level systems, institutions and policies. It will help ensure that SRHR and GBV services are planned, financed, delivered and monitored as an integrated, rights-based and government-owned system. The incumbent will work across health, social development, justice, education and protection structures, with particular attention to women, girls, adolescents, young people, persons with disabilities, LGBTQIA+ persons, Dalits and other populations left furthest behind.

The District Project Coordinator reports to the UNFPA Provincial Head. The incumbent receives technical guidance from UNFPA’s SRHR and Gender teams and collaborates closely with WHO, implementing partners and other members of the joint programme team.

How you can make a difference:

UNFPA is the lead United Nations agency for delivering a world where every pregnancy is intended, every childbirth is safe, and every young person’s potential is fulfilled. The UNFPA Strategic Plan for 2026-2029 articulates the organization’s response to a complex global environment, providing a roadmap for resilience and renewal. It is designed to accelerate the implementation of the Programme of Action of the International Conference on Population and Development (ICPD) and the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals by 2030. This mandate is pursued through a focus on four interconnected outcomes: ending the unmet need for family planning; ending preventable maternal deaths; ending gender-based violence and harmful practices; and adapting to demographic change through evidence and rights-based policies.

In a world where fundamental human rights are at risk, we need principled and ethical staff who embody these international norms and standards and will defend them courageously and with full conviction.

UNFPA is seeking candidates who transform, inspire, and deliver high-impact sustained results, ensuring effective external relations, communications, partnership-building and resource mobilization in a rapidly changing development and funding landscape. We need staff who are transparent, exceptional in how they manage the resources entrusted to them, and who commit to delivering excellence in programme results

Job Purpose:

The District Project Coordinator translates these outcomes into coordinated action at sub national levels. The District Project Coordinator will be working closely with local governments, district authorities, provincial government agencies, community organizations, development partners and other relevant stakeholders to ensure timely and effective delivery of planned results. The role combines policy advocacy and technical assistance, implementation coordination, service-system strengthening, community engagement, monitoring, reporting and learning, and humanitarian preparedness and response. It is expected to strengthen government ownership, mobilize co- financing from the local governments and private sector, and promote functional referral pathways and accountability for inclusive and integrated SRHR and GBV services in Nepal.

You would be responsible for:

1. Support policy advocacy, planning and budgeting process at Subnational Level

  • Provide hands-on support to assigned municipalities to integrate SRHR, GBV prevention and response, gender equality and social inclusion priorities into periodic and annual plans, sectoral plans, budgets and expenditure reviews.
  • Support evidence-based dialogue with elected representatives and government officials on mobilizing co-financing and prioritizing financial resources on integrated SRHR and GBV services, budget execution and government actions on essential services and frontline functions, including OCMCs, adolescent friendly health services, safe houses, case managers and community psychosocial services.
  • Help local governments to formulate effective laws and policy, policy implementation, and budget execution for improved access and quality and integrated SRHR and GBV services.
  • Support Municipality to harmonize the inter-departmental coordination and collaboration among the sections responsible for health, gender equality, education and finance.
  • Facilitate implementation of relevant national and subnational laws, policies, action plans, standards/SOPs and guidelines, including those related to integrated GBV and SRHR services, GESI, adolescent and youth health and humanitarian preparedness.
  • Support municipalities in implementing local-level policies and guidelines for integrated SRHR and GBV services.
  • Support municipalities to conduct periodic reviews, roll-out accountability tools and capacity building of Health Facility Operation and Management Committee on SRHR and its interlinkage with disaster GBV prevention and response.
  • Conduct advocacy activities with local government on cost sharing strategies for GBV and SRHR service provision and prioritizing gender responsive budgeting at local level.

2. Programme implementation support, coordination and quality assurance

  • Support the implementation of programme activities across assigned districts and municipalities in line with approved annual workplans, budgets, results frameworks, technical standards and partnership agreements.
  • Maintain regular liaison with local governments, district-level authorities, implementing partners, WHO, UNFPA technical and operations teams, health facilities with OCMC services, safe houses, schools, civil society organizations and community networks.
  • Provide day-to-day support to implementing partners and government counterparts in delivering planned activities, following up on implementation issues and facilitating timely completion of agreed actions.
  • Support monitoring of the quality and inclusiveness of training, orientations, dialogues, community initiatives and service-strengthening activities, ensuring alignment with rights-based, gender-transformative, survivor-centered, trauma-informed, adolescent-responsive and disability-inclusive approaches.
  • Participate in relevant networks and coordination mechanisms related to SRHR, GBV and the Protection Cluster, and support information sharing and coordination among relevant stakeholders.
  • Support municipalities and service providers to strengthen integrated SRHR and GBV service delivery, with a focus on OCMC services, safe houses and relevant justice and social services.
  • Support the mapping, periodic updating and practical use of multisectoral referral pathways linking communities, health facilities, hospitals, psychosocial support, safe accommodation, police, legal aid, justice and social protection services.
  • Provide day-to-day coordination, facilitation and operational support for programme activities.

3. Monitor, documentation and reporting of programme progress and results at the district level

  • Conduct regular field and joint monitoring visits to assess implementation, service quality, progress, and follow-up on corrective actions.
  • Document results, lessons, good practices, challenges, and risks; support learning, donor visits, and safe and ethical programme communications.

4. Risk management, safeguarding and humanitarian support

  • Promote a respectful, inclusive and safe working environment, and support partners and frontline personnel to understand and apply PSEA, prevention of sexual harassment, child safeguarding and other safeguarding requirements.
  • Support partners to provide communities with safe, accessible and confidential feedback and reporting channels, and promptly report any safeguarding concerns or allegations through the appropriate UNFPA channels.
  • Support coordination with provincial and district disaster-management authorities, health emergency structures, protection/GBV coordination mechanisms and humanitarian partners to strengthen preparedness and continuity of essential SRH and GBV services during emergencies.
  • Perform other duties within the scope of the position as required by the supervisor or UNFPA management.

5. Others

  • Create a safe working environment by developing respectful and safe organizational culture and supporting practices.
  • Perform any other duties as requested by the supervisor and the UNFPA Management team.

Qualifications and Experience:

Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Public Health, Nursing, Midwifery, Gender Studies, Sociology or other related field with 4 years of relevant experience OR Secondary-level education in above mentioned field with 7 years of relevant experience.

Knowledge and Experience:

  • Demonstrated experience in programme implementation, coordination, monitoring and reporting at provincial, district and municipal level.
  • Demonstrated knowledge and practical experience in at least one of the following areas, together with a sound working understanding of the other: sexual and reproductive health and rights; gender equality and gender-based violence prevention and response.
  • Experience working with local governments in Nepal, particularly health, gender, social development, justice, protection and planning.
  • Experience coordinating implementing partners, civil society organizations, service providers and multidisciplinary stakeholders.
  • Understanding of rights-based, survivor-centered, adolescent-responsive, disability-inclusive and Leave No One Behind approaches.
  • Experience with field monitoring, data quality assurance, referral systems, quality improvement or humanitarian preparedness and response is an advantage.
  • Familiarity with UNFPA’s mandate, the ICPD Programme of Action, Nepal’s federal governance system and relevant SRHR and GBV laws and policies is an advantage.
  • Prior experience with the United Nations or an international development organization is an asset.
  • Proficiency in standard office applications, including word processing, spreadsheets, presentations and digital collaboration tools.
  • Ability and willingness to travel frequently within the assigned province and to remote programme locations, subject to applicable security procedures.

Languages:

  • Fluency in English and Nepali (oral and written) is required. Knowledge of the local language(s) spoken in the district where the position is based will be an advantage.

Required Competencies:

Values:

  • Exemplifying integrity,
  • Demonstrating commitment to UNFPA and the UN system,
  • Embracing cultural diversity,
  • Embracing change.

Core Competencies:

  • Achieving results,
  • Being accountable,
  • Developing and applying professional expertise/business acumen,
  • Thinking analytically and strategically,
  • Working in teams/managing ourselves and our relationships.

Functional Competencies:

  • Business acumen,
  • Implementing management systems,
  • Innovation and marketing of new approaches,
  • Client orientation,
  • Organizational awareness.

Compensation and Benefits:

This position offers an attractive remuneration package including leave days, health insurance and additional remuneration for pensions and social security obligations.

UNFPA Work Environment:

UNFPA provides a work environment that reflects the values of gender equality, diversity, integrity and healthy work-life balance. We are committed to ensuring gender parity in the organization and therefore encourage women to apply. Individuals from the LGBTQIA+ community, minority ethnic groups, indigenous populations, persons with disabilities, and other underrepresented groups are highly encouraged to apply. Reasonable accommodation may be provided to applicants with disabilities upon request, to support their participation in the recruitment process. UNFPA promotes equal opportunities in terms of appointment, training, compensation and selection for all regardless of personal characteristics and dimensions of diversity. Diversity, Equity and Inclusion is at the heart of UNFPA’s workforce – click here to learn more.

Disclaimer:

Selection and engagement of LSC personnel may be subject to background and reference checks, medical clearance and other administrative requirements.

UNFPA does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or selection process and does not concern itself with information on applicants’ bank accounts.

It will help ensure that SRHR and GBV services are planned, financed, delivered and monitored as an integrated, rights-based and government-owned system. The incumbent will work across health, social development, justice, education and protection structures, with particular attention to women, girls, adolescents, young people, persons with disabilities, LGBTQIA+ persons, Dalits and other populations left furthest behind.

The District Project Coordinator reports to the UNFPA Provincial Head. The incumbent receives technical guidance from UNFPA’s SRHR and Gender teams and collaborates closely with WHO, implementing partners and other members of the joint programme team.

How you can make a difference:

UNFPA is the lead United Nations agency for delivering a world where every pregnancy is intended, every childbirth is safe, and every young person’s potential is fulfilled. The UNFPA Strategic Plan for 2026-2029 articulates the organization’s response to a complex global environment, providing a roadmap for resilience and renewal. It is designed to accelerate the implementation of the Programme of Action of the International Conference on Population and Development (ICPD) and the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals by 2030. This mandate is pursued through a focus on four interconnected outcomes: ending the unmet need for family planning; ending preventable maternal deaths; ending gender-based violence and harmful practices; and adapting to demographic change through evidence and rights-based policies.

In a world where fundamental human rights are at risk, we need principled and ethical staff who embody these international norms and standards and will defend them courageously and with full conviction.

UNFPA is seeking candidates who transform, inspire, and deliver high-impact sustained results, ensuring effective external relations, communications, partnership-building and resource mobilization in a rapidly changing development and funding landscape. We need staff who are transparent, exceptional in how they manage the resources entrusted to them, and who commit to delivering excellence in programme results

Job Purpose:

The District Project Coordinator translates these outcomes into coordinated action at sub national levels. The District Project Coordinator will be working closely with local governments, district authorities, provincial government agencies, community organizations, development partners and other relevant stakeholders to ensure timely and effective delivery of planned results. The role combines policy advocacy and technical assistance, implementation coordination, service-system strengthening, community engagement, monitoring, reporting and learning, and humanitarian preparedness and response. It is expected to strengthen government ownership, mobilize co- financing from the local governments and private sector, and promote functional referral pathways and accountability for inclusive and integrated SRHR and GBV services in Nepal.

You would be responsible for:

1. Support policy advocacy, planning and budgeting process at Subnational Level

  • Provide hands-on support to assigned municipalities to integrate SRHR, GBV prevention and response, gender equality and social inclusion priorities into periodic and annual plans, sectoral plans, budgets and expenditure reviews.
  • Support evidence-based dialogue with elected representatives and government officials on mobilizing co-financing and prioritizing financial resources on integrated SRHR and GBV services, budget execution and government actions on essential services and frontline functions, including OCMCs, adolescent friendly health services, safe houses, case managers and community psychosocial services.
  • Help local governments to formulate effective laws and policy, policy implementation, and budget execution for improved access and quality and integrated SRHR and GBV services.
  • Support Municipality to harmonize the inter-departmental coordination and collaboration among the sections responsible for health, gender equality, education and finance.
  • Facilitate implementation of relevant national and subnational laws, policies, action plans, standards/SOPs and guidelines, including those related to integrated GBV and SRHR services, GESI, adolescent and youth health and humanitarian preparedness.
  • Support municipalities in implementing local-level policies and guidelines for integrated SRHR and GBV services.
  • Support municipalities to conduct periodic reviews, roll-out accountability tools and capacity building of Health Facility Operation and Management Committee on SRHR and its interlinkage with disaster GBV prevention and response.
  • Conduct advocacy activities with local government on cost sharing strategies for GBV and SRHR service provision and prioritizing gender responsive budgeting at local level.

2. Programme implementation support, coordination and quality assurance

  • Support the implementation of programme activities across assigned districts and municipalities in line with approved annual workplans, budgets, results frameworks, technical standards and partnership agreements.
  • Maintain regular liaison with local governments, district-level authorities, implementing partners, WHO, UNFPA technical and operations teams, health facilities with OCMC services, safe houses, schools, civil society organizations and community networks.
  • Provide day-to-day support to implementing partners and government counterparts in delivering planned activities, following up on implementation issues and facilitating timely completion of agreed actions.
  • Support monitoring of the quality and inclusiveness of training, orientations, dialogues, community initiatives and service-strengthening activities, ensuring alignment with rights-based, gender-transformative, survivor-centered, trauma-informed, adolescent-responsive and disability-inclusive approaches.
  • Participate in relevant networks and coordination mechanisms related to SRHR, GBV and the Protection Cluster, and support information sharing and coordination among relevant stakeholders.
  • Support municipalities and service providers to strengthen integrated SRHR and GBV service delivery, with a focus on OCMC services, safe houses and relevant justice and social services.
  • Support the mapping, periodic updating and practical use of multisectoral referral pathways linking communities, health facilities, hospitals, psychosocial support, safe accommodation, police, legal aid, justice and social protection services.
  • Provide day-to-day coordination, facilitation and operational support for programme activities.

3. Monitor, documentation and reporting of programme progress and results at the district level

  • Conduct regular field and joint monitoring visits to assess implementation, service quality, progress, and follow-up on corrective actions.
  • Document results, lessons, good practices, challenges, and risks; support learning, donor visits, and safe and ethical programme communications.

4. Risk management, safeguarding and humanitarian support

  • Promote a respectful, inclusive and safe working environment, and support partners and frontline personnel to understand and apply PSEA, prevention of sexual harassment, child safeguarding and other safeguarding requirements.
  • Support partners to provide communities with safe, accessible and confidential feedback and reporting channels, and promptly report any safeguarding concerns or allegations through the appropriate UNFPA channels.
  • Support coordination with provincial and district disaster-management authorities, health emergency structures, protection/GBV coordination mechanisms and humanitarian partners to strengthen preparedness and continuity of essential SRH and GBV services during emergencies.
  • Perform other duties within the scope of the position as required by the supervisor or UNFPA management.

5. Others

  • Create a safe working environment by developing respectful and safe organizational culture and supporting practices.
  • Perform any other duties as requested by the supervisor and the UNFPA Management team.

Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Public Health, Nursing, Midwifery, Gender Studies, Sociology or other related field with 4 years of relevant experience OR Secondary-level education in above mentioned field with 7 years of relevant experience.

Knowledge and Experience:

  • Demonstrated experience in programme implementation, coordination, monitoring and reporting at provincial, district and municipal level.
  • Demonstrated knowledge and practical experience in at least one of the following areas, together with a sound working understanding of the other: sexual and reproductive health and rights; gender equality and gender-based violence prevention and response.

  • Proficiency in standard office applications, including word processing, spreadsheets, presentations and digital collaboration tools.
  • Ability and willingness to travel frequently within the assigned province and to remote programme locations, subject to applicable security procedures.

Posiiton: Health Emergency Associate Logistician
Duty Station: Rasuwa, Nuwakot
Work location: On UN premises
Expected start date: 14/09/2026
Duration: 3 months
(with possibility of extension)
Sustainable Development Goal: 3. Good health and well-being
Host entity: UNICEF
Modality: Onsite
Type: National
Volunteer category: Associate UCoS from Apr2026
Work schedule: Full-time
Number of Assignments: 2

Details

Mission and objectives

UNICEF promotes the rights and wellbeing of every child, in everything we do. Together with our partners, we work in 190 countries and territories to translate that commitment into practical action, focusing special effort on reaching the most vulnerable and excluded children, to the benefit of all children, everywhere.

In all of its work, UNICEF takes a life-cycle based approach, recognizing the particular importance of early childhood development and adolescence. UNICEF programmes focus on the most disadvantaged children, including those living in fragile contexts, those with disabilities, those who are affected by rapid urbanization and those affected by environmental degradation.

UNICEF was created with a distinct purpose in mind: to work with others to overcome the obstacles that poverty, violence, disease and discrimination place in a child’s path. We advocate for measures to give children the best start in life, because proper care at the youngest age forms the strongest foundation for a person’s future.

We promote girls’ education – ensuring that they complete primary education as a minimum – because it benefits all children, both girls and boys. Girls who are educated grow up to become better thinkers, better citizens, and better parents to their own children. We act so that all children are immunized against common childhood diseases, and are well nourished: no child should suffer or die from a preventable illness. We work to prevent the spread of HIV/AIDS among young people because it is right to keep them from harm and enable them to protect others. We help children and families affected by HIV/AIDS to live their lives with dignity.

We are UNICEF, the United Nations Children’s Fund.

Context

UNICEF Nepal Country Office (NCO) leads UNICEF’s health, nutrition, WASH, education, child protection and social policy programming in Nepal, working with the Government of Nepal, provincial and local governments, and humanitarian partners. Following the flash flood originating in the upper Bhotekoshi river system on 26 August 2026, which caused severe multi-sector damage across Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha, Chitwan and Tanahu districts, UNICEF is supporting the Ministry of Health and Food Safety (MoHFS), the Department of Health Services (DoHS), and District Health Offices in Rasuwa and Nuwakot to restore essential health services, sustain immunization (including Measles-Rubella catch-up and Oral Cholera Vaccine campaigns), and ensure the safe, traceable and timely delivery of health supplies and cold-chain items to flood-affected communities.

This UNV assignment is part of UNICEF Nepal’s Bhotekoshi-Rasuwa Flood Emergency Health Response, under the Health Section’s emergency surge deployment. The two UN Volunteers under this assignment will be based in the District Health Offices of Rasuwa and Nuwakot respectively, working alongside the District Disaster Management Committees (DDMCs), Local Disaster Management Committees (LDMCs) and UNICEF’s field emergency team to strengthen on-the-ground coordination, supply traceability and cold-chain/vaccine logistics for the health response

Task description

Within the delegated authority and under the supervision of the Immunization Specialist and the designated Emergency Health Focal Point, UNICEF Nepal Country Office or his/her designated mandated representative(s), the UNV Health Emergency Associate Logistician will:

  •  Serve as UNICEF’s on-the-ground focal point for health supply coordination at the District Health Office (DHO) and District/Local Disaster Management Committee (DDMC/LDMC) in the assigned district (Rasuwa or Nuwakot), facilitating onloading, registration of UNICEF supplies in the DDMC supply information management system (IMS), and stacking of supplies in a clearly identifiable, labelled UNICEF-designated location within government warehouses and/or any other alternative arrangements as may be desired during emergency.
  • Maintain an accurate, up-to-date tracking system (manual and/or digital) for all UNICEF health equipment, supplies, commodities, medicines and vaccines from receipt at the designated district warehouse through to final distribution point, to prevent commingling with other agencies’ or sectors’ supplies and to enable end-to-end traceability.
  • Consideration of first in/expiry, first out specially for perishable supplies to avoid wastage.
  • Support cold-chain management and logistics for immunizations, including monitoring of Ice-Lined Refrigerators (ILRs)/cold boxes, solar backup requirements, and coordination of vaccine transport to hard-to-reach holding centres and health facilities.
  • Liaise daily with other sectoral colleagues (Nutrition, WASH) and the District Health Office to identify immediate supply gaps at holding centres and health facilities and prioritize dispatch of UNICEF supplies accordingly.
  •  Support sector-wise packing and labelling of UNICEF supplies for onward transport (e.g., grouping health/cold-chain items separately from WASH, Education supplies), with clear, durable UNICEF visibility on each consignment.
  •  Compile and submit regular (at minimum weekly) supply status reports to the UNICEF Health Section and Supply & Logistics Unit, covering stock levels, dispatches, distribution, gaps and any constraints affecting delivery.
  • Support coordination between the District Health Office, Health Cluster/sub-national health coordination mechanisms, and UNICEF’s field emergency team on health logistics matters, including participation in relevant district- or local-level coordination meetings.
  • Coordinate the required activities with relevant local partners and communities.
  • Support onward field distribution planning and monitoring visits to holding centres and health facilities to verify receipt and appropriate use of UNICEF-supplied health items.
  • Any other related tasks as may be required or assigned by the supervisor.

Furthermore, UN Volunteers are encouraged to integrate the UN Volunteers programme mandate within their assignment and promote voluntary action through engagement with communities in the course of their work. As such, UN Volunteers should dedicate a part of their working time to some of the following suggested activities:

  • Strengthen their knowledge and understanding of the concept of volunteerism by reading relevant UNV and external publications and take active part in UNV activities (for instance in events that mark International Volunteer Day);
  • Be acquainted with and build on traditional and/or local forms of volunteerism in the host country;
  •  Provide annual and end of assignment self-reports on UN Volunteer actions, results and opportunities.
  •  Contribute articles/write-ups on field experiences and submit them for UNV publications/websites, newsletters, press releases, etc.;
  •  Assist with the UNV Buddy Programme for newly-arrived UN Volunteers;
  • Promote or advise local groups in the use of online volunteering or encourage relevant local individuals and organizations to use the UNV Online Volunteering service whenever technically possible.

17. Results/expected outputs:

  • As an active UNICEF team member, efficient, timely, responsive, client-friendly and high-quality support rendered to UNICEF and its beneficiaries in the accomplishment of her/his functions, including:
  •  UNICEF health equipment and supplies dispatched and installed to Rasuwa/Nuwakot are registered, traceable and distributed without commingling with other sectors’ or agencies’ supplies.
  •  Timely, accurate weekly supply status reports (stock, dispatch, distribution, gaps) submitted to the UNICEF Health Section and Supply & Logistics Unit.
  •  Cold-chain integrity maintained for immunization, vaccines transported and stored in the assigned district, with issues escalated and resolved promptly.
  • Age, Gender and Diversity (AGD) perspective is systematically applied, integrated and documented in all activities throughout the assignment
  • A final statement of achievements towards volunteerism for peace and development during the assignment, such as reporting on the number of volunteers mobilized, activities participated in and capacities developed

Eligibility criteria

Age: 18 – 80

Required experience: 1 month

Nationality: Candidate must be a national, legal resident or hold refugee status in the country of assignment.

Assignment requirements

Relevant experience

2 years

Languages

English, Level: Fluent, Required

Nepalese, Level: Fluent, Required

Required education level

  • Bachelor’s degree in public health, Pharmacy, Finance, Logistics, Business Administration or a related field

Competencies and values

  • Professionalism: demonstrated understanding of operations relevant to UNICEF; technical capabilities or knowledge relevant or transferrable to UNICEF procedures and rules; discretion, political sensitivity, diplomacy and tact to deal with clients; ability to apply good judgement; ability to liaise and coordinate with a range of different actors, especially in senior positions; where appropriate, high degree of autonomy, personal initiative and ability to take ownership; resourcefulness and willingness to accept wide responsibilities and ability to work independently under established procedures; ability to manage information objectively, accurately and confidentially; responsive and client-oriented;
  • Integrity: demonstrate the values and ethical standards of the UN and UNICEF in daily activities and behaviours while acting without consideration of personal gains; resist undue political pressure in decision-making; stand by decisions that are in the organization’s interest even if they are unpopular; take prompt action in cases of unprofessional or unethical behaviour; does not abuse power or authority;
  •  Teamwork and respect for diversity: ability to operate effectively across organizational boundaries; excellent interpersonal skills; ability to establish and maintain effective partnerships and harmonious working relations in a multi-cultural, multi-ethnic, mixed-gender environment with sensitivity and respect for diversity; sensitivity and adaptability to culture, gender, religion, nationality and age; commitment to implementing the goal of gender equality by ensuring the equal participation and full involvement of women and men in all aspects of UN operations; ability to achieve common goals and provide guidance or training to colleagues;
    • Commitment to continuous learning: initiative and willingness to learn new skills and stay abreast of new developments in area of expertise; ability to adapt to changes in work environment.
  • Planning and organizing: effective organizational and problem-solving skills and ability to manage a large volume of work in an efficient and timely manner; ability to establish priorities and to plan, coordinate and monitor (own) work; ability to work under pressure, with conflicting deadlines, and to handle multiple concurrent projects/activities;
  • Communication: proven interpersonal skills; good spoken and written communication skills, including ability to prepare clear and concise reports; ability to conduct presentations, articulate options and positions concisely; ability to make and defend recommendations; ability to communicate and empathize with staff (including national staff), military personnel, volunteers, counterparts and local interlocutors coming from very diverse backgrounds; capacity to transfer information and knowledge to a wide range of different target groups;
  • Flexibility: adaptability and ability to live and work in potentially hazardous and remote conditions, involving physical hardship and little comfort; to operate independently in austere environments for protracted periods; willingness to travel within the area of operations and to transfer to other duty stations within the area of operations as necessary;
  •  Genuine commitment towards the principles of voluntary engagement, which includes solidarity, compassion, reciprocity and self-reliance; and commitment towards UNICEF’s mission and vision, as well as to the UN Core Values.

Skills and experience

  • At least 2 years of professional work experience in health/medical supply chain management, cold-chain/vaccine logistics, warehousing or emergency logistics; experience with government supply information management systems (IMS) and/or UN/INGO logistics systems is an asset, as is prior experience working in the UN or other international development/humanitarian organization;
  •  Working knowledge of vaccine cold-chain management (ILRs, cold boxes, temperature monitoring) is highly desirable; familiarity with DDMC/LDMC coordination structures and the Nepal health system is an asset;
  • Excellent oral and written skills; excellent drafting, formulation, reporting skills;
  •  Accuracy and professionalism in document production and editing;
  •  Excellent interpersonal skills; culturally and socially sensitive; ability to work inclusively and collaboratively with a range of partners, including grassroots community members, religious and youth organizations, and authorities at different levels; familiarity with tools and approaches of communications for development;
  • Ability to work and adapt professionally and effectively in a challenging environment; ability to work effectively in a multicultural team of international and national personnel;
  •  Solid overall computer literacy, including proficiency in various MS Office applications (Excel, Word, etc.) and email/internet; familiarity with database management; and office technology equipment;
  • Self-motivated, ability to work with minimum supervision; ability to work with tight deadlines;
  • Desirable: valid national driver’s license and proven ability to drive manual gear 4×4 over rough terrain; (if not applicable, delete)
  •  Sound security awareness;
  • Have affinity with or interest in public health, humanitarian logistics and emergency response, volunteerism as a mechanism for durable development, and the UN System

Area(s) of expertise

Emergency preparedness, crisis response, Logistics, procurement, commodities

Driving license
–

Other information

Volunteerism is understood as a wide range of activities undertaken of free will, for the general public good, for which monetary reward is not the principal motivating factor.

Living conditions and remarks

The assignment is based in Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts, Bagmati Province — areas severely affected by the 26 August 2026 Bhotekoshi-Rasuwa flash flood. Road access remains disrupted in parts of both districts, with some areas reachable only by foot, zip-line ropeway or air; travel times and conditions may change as repair works progress. Basic accommodation, food, water and electricity are available in district headquarters (Dhunche, Bidur) but may be intermittent; mobile network and internet connectivity can be unreliable, particularly in areas across the Trishuli River. Health facilities in the districts have sustained damage, and referral to Kathmandu may be required for serious medical needs. Given the hardship conditions and the physically demanding nature of fieldwork (including travel over rough terrain and, at times, extended periods away from the duty station), this is classified as a non-family assignment.

As this is a national UN Volunteer assignment, the UN Volunteer will be responsible for arranging his/her own housing and other living essentials.

Inclusivity statement

United Nations Volunteers is an equal opportunity programme that welcomes applications from qualified professionals. We are committed to achieving diversity in terms of gender, care protected characteristics. As part of their adherence to the values of UNV, all UN Volunteers commit themselves to combat any form of discrimination, and to promoting respect for human rights and individual dignity, without distinction of a person’s race, sex, gender identity, religion, nationality, ethnic origin, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, age, language, social origin or other status.

Reasonable accommodation

UNICEF offers reasonable accommodation for UN Volunteers with disabilities. This may include, for example, accessible software, travel assistance for missions or personal attendants. We encourage you to disclose your disability during your application in case you need reasonable accommodation during the recruitment process and afterwards in your assignment.

Note on Covid-19 vaccination requirements

In addition to duty station-specific vaccine requirements, appointments are subject to confirmation of fully-vaccinated status against SARS-CoV-2 (Covid-19) with a World Health Organization (WHO)-endorsed vaccine, which must be met prior to taking up the appointment. It does not apply to UN Volunteers who will work remotely and are not expected to work on or visit UNICEF premises, programme delivery locations or directly interact with communities UNICEF works with, nor to travel to perform functions for UNICEF for the duration of their contracts.

Scam warning

The United Nations does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process. Should you receive a solicitation for the payment of a fee, please disregard it. Furthermore, please note that emblems, logos, names and addresses are easily copied and reproduced. Therefore, you are advised to apply particular care when submitting personal information on the web.

title.rendered: Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Officer

content.rendered:
Position: Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) Officer
Project: Humanitarian Support (MHPSS)
Organization: KOSHISH
Duty Station: Bidur, Nuwakot, Nepal (with frequent field travel to project implementation areas)
Employment Type: Short-Term Employment (Six months )
Reports To: Humanitarian Manager

1. Background

KOSHISH is a national non-governmental organization established in 2008, dedicated to promoting mental health and psychosocial well-being in Nepal. KOSHISH is implementing emergency mental health and psychosocial support interventions for flood-affected communities with the support from multiple donors funded projects.

To ensure quality implementation, evidence-based decision-making, accountability to affected populations, and continuous learning, KOSHISH seeks a qualified Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Officer to support project monitoring, data management, reporting, accountability mechanisms, learning documentation, and compliance with donor requirements.

2. Job Purpose

The MEAL Officer will be responsible for establishing and implementing monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning systems for the humanitarian response project. The position will ensure timely collection, analysis, verification, and reporting of project data, facilitate beneficiary feedback and complaints mechanisms, support evidence-based decision-making, and promote organizational learning while ensuring compliance with KOSHISH and donor MEAL requirements.

3. Major Duties and Responsibilities

  • Develop and implement project monitoring plans, Assessment tools, trackers, and reporting systems in humanitarian setting .
  • Conduct field monitoring visits to assess project progress, quality, effectiveness, and compliance.
  • Collect, verify, clean, manage, and maintain accurate project and beneficiary data.
  • Track project indicators against targets and ensure timely collection of output, outcome, and impact data.
  • Support baseline studies, assessments, post-distribution monitoring (PDM), and endline evaluations.
  • Analyze quantitative and qualitative data to generate insights and evidence for program improvement.
  • Prepare monitoring reports, dashboards, presentations, and donor-required reporting documentation.
  • Establish and manage beneficiary feedback and complaint-response mechanisms, ensuring timely resolution.
  • Promote accountability, inclusion, participation, safeguarding, and confidentiality in all project activities.
  • Document lessons learned, best practices, case studies, and support organizational learning initiatives.
  • Facilitate review meetings, reflection sessions, and adaptive management through evidence-based recommendations.
  • Ensure data quality through verification, validation, audits, spot checks, and adherence to data standards.
  • Support staff on the proper use of monitoring tools, data collection systems, and information management protocols.
  • Coordinate with program, finance, procurement, and administrative teams, and support donor visits, audits, and assessments.
  • Ensure compliance with organizational policies, MEAL standards, safeguarding requirements, donor guidelines, and perform other assigned project-related duties.

4. Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Public Health, Social Sciences, Development Studies, Information Management or related disciplines.
  • Specialized training in Monitoring and Evaluation, Research Methods, Data Analysis, MIS, or Humanitarian Accountability will be an added advantage.

Professional Experience

  • Minimum 2 years of relevant professional experience in Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL), project monitoring, data management, or research within NGO/INGO or humanitarian programmes.
  • Experience in conducting surveys, assessments, monitoring visits, and data verification in humanitarian setting.
  • Demonstrated experience with data collection tools such as KoboToolbox, ODK, CommCare, SurveyCTO, or similar platforms.
  • Experience in data analysis using Excel, Power BI, SPSS, or similar software.
  • Experience in humanitarian response, disaster risk reduction, MHPSS, protection, or emergency programmes will be highly preferred.
  • Knowledge of donor reporting requirements and MEAL frameworks.
  • Experience in community engagement, feedback mechanisms, and accountability systems is desirable.

5. Required Competencies

  • Strong understanding of MEAL principles and humanitarian accountability standards.
  • Knowledge of logical frameworks, indicators, results-based management, and data quality assurance.
  • Excellent data analysis and reporting skills.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and digital data collection platforms.
  • Ability to develop monitoring tools and reporting templates.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • High level of integrity, confidentiality, and professionalism.
  • Ability to work under pressure and meet tight deadlines.
  • Commitment to humanitarian principles and safeguarding standards.
  • Ability to work effectively with diverse stakeholders and communities

(Note: Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Original documents must be presented during the interview or prior to appointment for verification.)

Salary: Negotiable as per competence and experience.

Applying Procedure:

Interested candidates are requested to send a Cover letter and updated CV in recruit@koshish.org.np .

We will be reviewing the applications on a Rolling Basis, however the last date to submit your application is 20th September 2026.

Note:

Eligible candidates with disabilities, women and from the local area are encouraged to apply. We are committed to ensuring the safety, dignity, and well-being of all individuals and maintains zero tolerance for sexual exploitation, abuse, harassment, or any other form of harm. All shortlisted candidates will be required to comply with KOSHISH’s Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct and will undergo appropriate safeguarding checks KOSHISH reserves the right to accept or reject any or all applications without assigning any reason

Posiiton: Operations Manager, Flash Flood Response
Location: Kathmandu, Nepal

End Date: September 22, 2026

With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 31,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

Employee Contract Type:

Local – Fixed Term Employee (Fixed Term)

Job Description:

The Operation Manager will lead the implementation of the Nepal Flash Flood Response projects in Rasuwa and Nuwakot, ensuring timely, quality and accountable delivery in line with the approved response plan, donor requirements and WVI Nepal’s strategy.

The role will oversee multi-sector humanitarian interventions, provide guidance and quality assurance to Partner NGOs, and lead coordination with local governments, donors, UN agencies and other stakeholders. The incumbent will ensure effective project planning, reporting, financial and supply chain management, monitoring, compliance and team coordination, while using data and evidence to support timely decisions and adaptive management.

The role will also promote staff well-being, safety and safeguarding and work closely with Finance, MEAL, Communications and other support functions to ensure effective response delivery and early recovery.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

Response Project Leadership and Management

  • Lead and oversee the implementation of all Nepal Flash Flood Response projects across Nuwakot and Rasuwa districts in accordance with approved response plans, donor requirements, government agreements, and WVI Nepal policies and standards.
  • Ensure timely, quality and accountable delivery of project activities across all response sectors including Food Assistance, Shelter and NFI, Cash and Voucher Assistance (CVA), WASH, Health and Nutrition, Education, Child Protection, and Livelihood Recovery.
  • Develop and maintain integrated implementation plans, district work plans, spending projections and response milestones to ensure achievement of project targets and outcomes.
  • Provide operational leadership and timely decision-making to address implementation challenges, emerging risks, and changing humanitarian needs.
  • Ensure response activities contribute to the recovery and resilience of affected communities while supporting alignment with WVI Nepal’s long-term programming and strategic objectives.
  • Support the Response Manager with analysis, planning, strategic recommendations, and operational monthly report and updates to facilitate evidence-based decision making.
  • Periodic reports are generated and are disseminated timely and effectively.

District Operation and Team Management

  • Provide direct supervision, coaching and performance management to district-based response staff and the Rasuwa District Coordinator.
  • Lead and coordinate multidisciplinary response teams across both districts to ensure effective collaboration, communication, accountability, and achievement of project objectives.

Program Quality, Monitoring, Accountability and Learning

Government, Community and External Coordination

  • Represent World Vision at district-level coordination forums, government meetings, cluster mechanisms, humanitarian working groups and partner engagements as delegated by the Response Manager.

    Lead budget revision if needed with appropriate rationale.

KNOWLEDGE/QUALIFICATIONS FOR THE ROLE

Required Professional Experience

  • At least 5 years management experience in national and/or international NGOs, including grants management.
  • Demonstrated depth of experience and expertise preferably in an NGO context in working with community/grassroots people and organizations, specially focusing on DRR.

  • Management and organizational development for staff, communities and government stakeholders.

  • Strategic, creative, and innovative thinking, solves problems with prudent decision making. Effective people management with emotional intelligence.

Required Education, training, license, registration and certification

Oxfam has been working in Nepal for over 40 years. We implement programmes through three interrelated thematic priorities – Climate and Water, Gender Justice, and Humanitarian and DRM to respond to the intersectional and multidimensional nature of inequalities and injustices that perpetuate poverty in the lives of women, marginalized, vulnerable people and communities

The Role

To form part of the Oxfam emergency response team, providing technical and operational support to assess, analyse and respond to the food security, cash and livelihood needs of communities affected by flash floods in Nepal.

The EFSVL Officer will work closely with Oxfam teams, partners, communities and relevant stakeholders to support the rapid assessment, design, implementation and monitoring of EFSVL and cash-based interventions. The role will focus on ensuring that assistance is timely, appropriate, inclusive, accountable and responsive to the evolving needs of affected communities.

Key responsibilities include supporting needs and market assessments; contributing to response planning and programme design; providing technical support to partners and field teams; supporting beneficiary identification and registration; facilitating cash or voucher distributions where appropriate; monitoring markets, prices and programme quality; and ensuring that community feedback and learning inform ongoing response decisions. The Officer will work closely with MEAL, Finance, Logistics, Procurement, WASH, Protection, Gender and other programme teams to ensure effective coordination, information sharing and efficient use of resources. The role will also support field-level problem solving, documentation, reporting and early recovery planning, with a strong emphasis on partner capacity strengthening and quality assurance.

Who we’re looking for
We are looking for someone who has the following experience, knowledge and competencies.

Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in social sciences, Agriculture, Rural Development, Economics, Business, Food Security, Livelihoods or another relevant discipline from a recognized institution.

Experience & Skills:

  • 3-5 years of relevant experience demonstrated technical experience in one or more key EFSVL areas, particularly cash and voucher assistance, food security, livelihoods, agricultural assistance and market-based programming.
  • Proven experience in cash and voucher programming, including beneficiary targeting and registration, distribution/payment mechanisms, use of digital tools and systems, and programme tracking and monitoring.
  • Experience conducting food security, livelihoods and market assessments, analysing data and using findings to inform response analysis, programme design, transfer values and implementation approaches. Experience with market assessment methodologies such as EMMA is an advantage.
  • Demonstrated experience of working through and strengthening local partners, including providing technical guidance, coaching, mentoring and hands-on support to improve programme quality and delivery capacity.
  • Experience managing partnerships effectively, including the ability to build trust, influence without direct authority, resolve implementation challenges and ensure agreed activities are delivered to required standards.
  • Experience working in emergency and rapidly changing environments, with the ability to adapt programme approaches to evolving needs, risks, market conditions and operational constraints.
  • Attention to detail and good organisational and administrative skills, including the ability to present concise reports, sometimes a short notice, reflecting the problems and possible solutions for particular situations.
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills and the ability to effectively manage and demonstrate leadership within a diverse and multi-cultural team.
  • Clear understanding of, and commitment to, the aims and objectives of Oxfam and humanitarian protection standards and Oxfam Codes of Conduct, the Sphere Minimum Standards, gender, equity and diversity principles.
  • Strong oral and written communication ability in English and relevant local language, and computer literacy.

What we offer

This role will provide you with an opportunity to make a difference in Oxfam by working closely with a group of passionate people that are specialists in their field of Gender, WASH and Water Governance, Humanitarian and DRM and so forth along with the national and international training and development opportunities. Our offer consists of fair pay and competitive benefits package. At Oxfam, we believe that every aspect of our work can lead to a positive outcome. If you have the same opinion, together with the ability to meet the challenges involved, this role offers scope for immense personal fulfilment – as well as outstanding opportunities to develop your career.

Oxfam is committed to providing a fair compensation package and to providing a flexible, supportive, working environment.

How to apply

As part of your online application, please upload your up-to-date CV and Cover Letter explaining your suitability against the essential criteria in the job profile. Please click in apply.

REMOTE Internship: Research Intern – Neuroscience, Learning and AI in Higher Education
🏠 Remote
💵 $550 per month
👥 UNU-Macau

Job description

About UN University (UNU)

The United Nations University (UNU) is an international community of scholars engaged in policy-oriented research, capacity development and dissemination of knowledge, furthering the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations. UNU’s mission is to contribute, through research and capacity building, to efforts to resolve the pressing global problems that are the concern of the United Nations and its Member States.

For the past four decades, United Nations University (UNU) has been a go-to think tank for impartial research on human survival, conflict prevention, sustainable development and welfare. With more than 400 researchers in 12 countries, UNU’s work spans the 17 Sustainable Development Goals, generating policy-relevant knowledge to effect positive global change. UNU maintains more than 200 collaborations with UN agencies and leading universities and research institutions across the globe.

About UNU Institute in Macau (UNU Macau)

UNU Institute in Macau (UNU Macau) is one of 13 research and training Institutes that comprise the think tanks in the UNU system. UNU Macau is a research institute at the intersections of digital technology and sustainable development. The Institute conducts policy-relevant research and generates solutions, addressing pressing challenges expressed in the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development through high-impact innovations and the latest technologies. Through its research, the UNU Institute in Macau encourages data-driven and evidence-based actions and policies to contribute to the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals.

One of the Institute’s missions is to nurture the next generation of interdisciplinary computing, information and social scientists, and engineers to be leaders in the field of ICT for development. To this end, the institute seeks to build a team of experts to help deliver the institute’s mission and work plan. The Institute’s research tends to be more applied, and strives for policy impact in the UN system, at international, regional and national levels.

The UNU Institute in Macau is situated in the Macau Special Administrative Region (SAR) of China, and it is the only UN entity in the city. Macau is one of the most dynamic regions in Asia, where technological innovations have become an integral part in driving social and economic change. Macau is part of the Greater Bay Area (GBA), that hosts many private sector companies and technological giants that are just a short distance away. Its proximity to China, Hong Kong SAR and other Asian countries such as Japan, Korea, Thailand and Vietnam, provides an exciting opportunity for researchers and experts to maximize the impact of their work.

Responsibilities

Under the supervision of the Institute Director, the Research Intern – Neuroscience, Learning and AI in Higher Education will contribute to ongoing research for a forthcoming Springer publication on AI and higher education, as well as related policy and knowledge products. Responsibilities of the intern include:

  • Conduct literature reviews and research on neuroscience, learning, education, and AI in higher education.
  • Support research and analysis for the forthcoming Springer book on AI and higher education.
  • Explore how insights from neuroscience and learning science can inform educational policy and practice.
  • Contribute to policy outputs and recommendations, including the use of neuroscience-informed approaches in educational policymaking.
  • Draft and contribute to blogs, research papers, journal articles, and other knowledge products.
  • Support the preparation, organization, and analysis of research materials and evidence.

Expected Outputs

The intern is expected to contribute to:

  • Research briefs and literature reviews;
  • Policy recommendations on neuroscience, learning, and education;
  • Blog articles and other public-facing outputs;
  • Drafts or contributions to journal articles and academic publications;
  • Research and analysis contributing to the Springer book on AI and higher education.

Learning Objectives

The intern will gain experience in policy-oriented social science research within a UN research environment. Learning objectives include:

  • Strengthening research skills
  • Developing the ability to translate research findings into policy-relevant outputs
  • Gaining experience of working in the UN
  • Learning how to work in a multi-cultural environment

Competencies

Core Values:

  • Respect for Diversity
  • Integrity
  • Professionalism

Core Competencies:

  • Awareness and Sensitivity Regarding Gender Issues
  • Accountability
  • Creative Problem Solving
  • Effective Communication
  • Inclusive Collaboration

Qualifications

Education:

  • Master’s degree or above in neuroscience, education, learning sciences, psychology, AI, social sciences, or a related field.

Experience and Skills:

  • Strong research, analytical, and academic writing skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to conduct literature reviews and synthesize academic research.
  • Strong interest in the intersection of neuroscience, learning, AI, and higher education.
  • Ability to work independently and effectively in a remote environment.

Language:

  • Excellent written and spoken English.
  • Working knowledge of another UN language is an advantage.

Stipend
N/A

Duration of contract:

The duration of the internship is 2 months.  Anticipated from October 05 (Monday) to December 04 (Friday), 2026

Expected start date: October 05, 2026

How to Apply:

Application Procedure

Interested candidates should submit their application containing:

1) Brief cover letter (in English) stating interest in and qualifications for the post;

2) Current and complete CV in English;

3) Examples of relevant research work in English.

Candidates invited for interview must submit prior to the interview the following documents:

1) Document(s) confirming your education status (e.g. transcript or proof of enrollment);

2) Proof of health and life/accident insurance valid for the duration and location in which the internship will be carried out. Selected intern must have health and life insurance.

Application Deadline: September 18, 2026 (11:59pm, Macau time zone GMT +8)

** Application page no longer operational beyond application deadline.

Assessment
Evaluation of qualified candidates may include a desk review and/or a competency-based interview, and references.

Special notice
This is a remote internship. UNU does not sponsor a working visa for this position.

The purpose of the Internship Programme is not to lead to further employment with UNU but to complement an intern’s studies. Therefore, there should be no expectation of employment at the end of an internship.

Interns may not represent UNU in any official capacity. Interns do not hold international civil servant status nor are they considered a “staff member” as defined in the United Nations Staff Rules and Regulations.
UNU accepts no responsibility for costs arising from accidents and/or illness or death incurred during the internship.

UNU is committed to diversity and inclusion within its workforce, and encourages all candidates, irrespective of gender, nationality, religious and ethnic backgrounds, including persons living with disabilities to apply. Applications from developing countries, and from women are strongly encouraged.

UNU has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UNU, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination.

Scam warning
UNU does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process. Should you receive a solicitation for the payment of a fee, please disregard it. Furthermore, please note that emblems, logos, names and addresses are easily copied and reproduced. Therefore, you are advised to apply particular care when submitting personal information on the web.

Posiiton: Programme Coordinator

Location: Nuwakot

End Date: September 21, 2026

With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 31,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

Employee Contract Type:

Local – Fixed Term Employee (Fixed Term)

Job Description:

World Vision International Nepal (WVI Nepal) has launched a Category II Emergency Response in the priority districts of Rasuwa and Nuwakot, Bagmati Province, following devastating flash floods along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river corridors that caused casualties, displacement and extensive damage across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading. The 12-month Nepal Flash Flood Response (NFFR) 2026 plan targets 25,000 people, including 10,000 children, from around 5,000 affected households across seven sectors, moving from relief into early recovery.

The Programme Coordinator leads the Programmes function of the Nepal Flash Flood Response 2026 accountable for ensuring the response is designed, planned, monitored, evidenced and adapted on the basis of humanitarian need. The role works closely with WVI Nepal’s partners and leads response planning and design, the MEAL system, information management and reporting, and humanitarian accountability, and manages resource allocation and funding tracking with Finance. Grant acquisition sits outside the role, which supports it with evidence and technical content and leads donor and Support Office reporting. The position line manages the MEAL Officer and Information Management Officer.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

A. Response Planning and Programme Design

  • Facilitate response planning and program design with the Response Manager, operations, sector coordinators, PDQD and MEAL, and write, consolidate and disseminate the response plan and its revisions as needs evolve and the response moves from relief to recovery.
  • Ensure the design meets international humanitarian standards (Sphere, CHS) and World Vision guidance, and maintain the response logframe and indicators, including Disaster
  • Management core indicators so that sector plans trace to the three response outcomes.
  • Engage internal teams, clusters, government actors and current and potential partners on planning and design, identifying partnering opportunities and supporting local civil society.
  • With Operations and Partnering, set partner selection criteria aligned to program goals and donor requirements, and review partner proposals and budgets.
    Lead transition and phase-out planning, integrating response learning into WVI Nepal’s regular programming.

B. Resource Allocation, Funding Tracking, Grant Management and Compliance

  • With Finance and the Response Manager, keep the funding matrix aligned with PBAS, follow up commitments with Finance, and support the allocation process with Finance, the Response Manager and Operations so allocations reflect strategic priorities and comply with donor rules.
  • Provide evidence, needs analysis, logframes and indicators for proposals
  • Prepare the Project Agreement (PA) for the Social Welfare Council and lead all SWC reporting, including presenting progress at CPAC meetings.
  • Support Operations and partners to maintain grant management and compliance systems, start-up orientation, reporting schedules, grant health tracking, compliance monitoring and amendment requests ,and ensure partners meet each grant’s requirements.
  • Strengthen partner capacity in grant management, compliance and reporting, and in grant acquisition where opportunities arise.
  • Communicate humanitarian needs from assessments, monitoring and community feedback to Support Offices, with the Response Manager and the External Engagement Coordinator.

C. Assessment, Monitoring and Evaluation

  • Support the MEAL Officer to design and deliver needs assessments (food security, nutrition, market, livelihood, protection) and analyze findings for planning and adaptation and engage in inter-agency and joint assessments as agreed with Response Management.
  • Oversee the response monitoring system (CommCare, KoBo, World Vision and donor requirements) and support the MEAL Officer to produce monthly ITT reports for Operations and review partner logframes, MEAL plans and ITTs.
  • Support the MEAL Officer to run distribution and post-distribution monitoring across all districts and to manage baselines, real-time evaluations, reviews and the end-of-response evaluation, using findings and action plans to adapt programming.
  • Ensure MEAL and Information Management disaggregate data by sex, age and disability (Washington Group Short Set, WG/UNICEF Child Functioning Module), that at least two disability-specific outputs carry indicators, and that the 3% minimum participation rate is tracked.
  • Coordinate NEAT+ environmental screening with mitigation measures reflected in monitoring frameworks and take part in partner due diligence and capacity assessment, addressing medium and high MEAL risks and building partner MEAL capacity.
  • Coordinate joint monitoring with Local Government and the Social Welfare Council, manage third-party monitoring, and ensure MEAL staff handle and escalate sensitive disclosures in line with data protection standards.

D. Information Management and Reporting

  • Support to maintain the information management system as the single source of current response information and keep the WVI Relief Portal updated and information shared with the team.
  • Support to organize internal data (assessments, monitoring, feedback, context) and external data (NDRRMA, OCHA, clusters) into analysis and recommendations for Response Management.
  • Support to prepare internal and external reports with MEAL, Communications and Operations, Situation Reports, monitoring and cluster and donor (DFAT) reports.
  • Support to plan and manage donor, Support Office and Social Welfare Council reporting so that all requirements and deadlines are met, including integration of partner reports.
  • Set coordination-meeting reporting procedures and internal communications protocols so decisions are shared across the response team.

E. Humanitarian Accountability, GEDSI and Safeguarding

  • Support the MEAL function to run accessible community information, consultation, feedback and complaint mechanisms — based on community preference and able to receive confidential reports — and to log, answer analyze and share feedback with Operations, Response Management and partners within agreed timeframes.
  • Escalate all level 2 and 3 safeguarding incidents to the focal point within 24 hours, and ensure communities know expected staff behavior and how to report violations.
  • Ensure program design builds on local capacities, maximizes participation of the most vulnerable, and applies GEDSI and accountability standards in every sector plan, including the twin-track approach and engagement with Organizations of Persons with Disabilities.

F. Team Leadership, Learning and Function Management

  • Manage line, coach and develop the MEAL Officer and the Information Management Officer, including performance planning, review against quality criteria, and staff care.
  • Set the program function staffing plan with People & Culture, support recruitment, deployment and handovers, and develop the function budget with Finance.
  • Hold quality planning sessions, report achievement against quality criteria monthly, and escalate risks to delivery.
  • Capture and share lessons learned, run the national lessons-learned workshop and virtual learning event before handover, and integrate learning into WVI Nepal programming.
  • Work in line with the WVI Emergency Management System manual and the WVI Nepal DRR & HEA Guideline.
  • Undertake other duties as assigned by the Response Manager.

KNOWLEDGE/QUALIFICATIONS FOR THE ROLE

Required Professional Experience

  • Minimum five years’ professional experience in humanitarian or development programming, of which at least two years in an emergency response in a programmes, MEAL or information management role.
  • Demonstrated experience leading response planning and programme design against humanitarian needs, including writing response plans, logframes and indicator frameworks.
  • Proven experience designing and running MEAL systems in an emergency, including needs assessments, indicator tracking, post-distribution monitoring, real-time evaluation and evaluation management.
  • Practical command of digital data collection and analysis tools – KoBo Toolbox, CommCare, Power BI or equivalent – and strong Excel skills.
  • Working knowledge of the humanitarian cluster system, the National Disaster Response Framework, NDRRMA and DDMC coordination arrangements in Nepal.
  • Sound understanding of Sphere, the Core Humanitarian Standard, humanitarian accountability, safeguarding and PSEAH, Do No Harm and GEDSI/disability inclusion, including the Washington Group question sets.
  • Experience managing implementing partners, including capacity assessment, capacity building and joint monitoring.
  • Proven people-management experience and the ability to work effectively in a fast-moving, multi-stakeholder response environment.

Required Education, training, license, registration and certification

  • Master’s degree in development studies, social sciences, public health, disaster risk management, statistics or a related field; or a Bachelor’s degree with an additional two years of relevant experience.

Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications

  • Prior experience in a World Vision emergency response and familiarity with the Emergency Management System (EMS), the WVI Relief Portal, PBAS, LMMS and Disaster Management core indicators.
  • Experience with cash and voucher programming monitoring and market assessment.
  • Experience with NEAT+ environmental screening.
  • Certification or formal training in humanitarian programme cycle management, MEAL, or humanitarian information management.
  • Experience supporting institutional donor proposals and reporting (DFAT, UN agencies) even where acquisition is led by others.
  • Familiarity with the Bagmati Province context and working relationships with local government in Rasuwa and Nuwakot.

Work Base: Nuwakot District

Duration: One year

Travel and/or Work Environment

Extensive travel to Rasuwa and Nuwakot of up to 40% of working time. Field travel may involve difficult road conditions, disrupted access, remote locations and basic accommodation.

Physical Requirements

Willingness and physical ability to travel to Rasuwa and Nuwakot, including remote and disaster-affected locations, for up to 40% of working time.

Language Requirements

Excellent written and spoken English and Nepali, with a demonstrated ability to write reports for donors and external stakeholders.

Bagmati Welfare Society Nepal (BWSN) is a women-led and youth-led feminist organization established in 1995 in Sarlahi, Nepal. For thirty-two years BWSN has worked in the districts where public systems arrived last, and currently works across 201 local levels in Madhesh, Koshi, Lumbini, Karnali and Bagmati Provinces. Its work is organized around three pillars — People, Planet and Power: human wellbeing and social development, climate resilience and biodiversity, and inclusive governance and civic engagement.

The Response

On 26 August 2026, an ice-rock collapse near the Nepal–China border blocked the Lhende Khola. The lake that formed behind the blockage breached and sent a flash flood down the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers. There were no rainfall and no warning, and the Syabrubesi gauging station was destroyed in the flood. The Government of Nepal has declared 15 local levels across five districts disaster crisis-hit for three months under Section 32(1) of the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act, 2074.
