Job Description

BACKGROUND

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion are core principles at UNDP: we value diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate, we foster inclusion as a way of ensuring all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, and we ensure equity and fairness in all our actions. Taking a ‘leave no one behind’ approach to our diversity efforts means increasing representation of underserved populations. People who identify as belonging to marginalized or excluded populations are strongly encouraged to apply. Learn more about working at UNDP including our values and inspiring stories.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the development arm of the United Nations. Present in 170 countries with over 17,000 people, UNDP works on the world’s biggest problems: extreme poverty, climate change, good governance, renewable energy, crisis prevention, and women’s empowerment, among others.

Global development is increasingly shaped by interconnected crises, rapid technological change, and growing uncertainty. At the same time, digital technologies and artificial intelligence are transforming economies, governance systems, and public services, creating new opportunities to accelerate sustainable development when applied in inclusive and responsible ways.

As the development arm of the United Nations, UNDP serves as the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development and acts as the integrator for collective action to advance the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Working in over 170 countries and territories, UNDP’s policy and programme work spans global, regional, and national levels, linking deep local knowledge with cutting-edge global expertise in support of the UNDP Strategic Plan 2026–2029. Within this institutional framework, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) leads the development of corporate policies, technical guidance, and operational frameworks to advance UNDP’s mandate.

The Strategic Plan and the organization’s Digital Strategy recognize digitalization, data, and innovation as key accelerators for achieving development outcomes. These frameworks position digital and AI as foundational enablers for stronger institutions, evidence-based decision-making, and more effective service delivery.

Within this institutional context, the Digital, AI and Innovation (DAI) Hub serves as UNDP’s central platform for advancing systems transformation, inclusive digitalization, and innovation across its development work. The Hub brings together expertise in systems transformation, digital public infrastructure, data and artificial intelligence, bottom-up innovation, capacity development, and digital product design. Through an integrated approach, the Hub supports countries and UNDP teams to design integrated, scalable solutions that respond to both immediate development needs and long-term structural challenges.

By combining global expertise with field-based insight and strong partnerships, the DAI Hub contributes to UNDP’s mandate to deliver more agile, inclusive, and future-ready development solutions.

Please note that the start date for the internship is flexible, and needs-based. We will be receiving applications on a rolling basis until September 30th, 2026, and successful applicants can expect to hear back any time between April and the end of 2026.

Please read the instructions carefully to complete your application – applications are to be submitted both via the UNDP Vacancy Link AND the Airtable link: https://airtable.com/appeKAJ7quPABAfoc/pagj4yv4UGVuveqXx/form

 DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

We are looking for motivated interns who can support our work in any of the following areas listed below:

Systems Transformation & Innovation

Research & Knowledge Management

COMPETENCIES

Position: Field Officer
Duty Station: Morang, Sunsari and Udayapur, with frequent field visits

About Us:

Tarangini Mahila Adhikar Prashikshyen Kendra (Tarangini Foundation), established in 2017, is a feminist organisation dedicated to advancing gender justice through advocacy, documentation and movement-building. Our work is rooted in the belief that women’s bodies, identity and work are central pillars of their agency and autonomy for realizing their rights, as well as for social transformation. We aim to make women’s work visible, challenge structural inequalities, and strengthen the feminist movement in Nepal.

About the Role:

The Field Officer is responsible for supporting the effective implementation of program activities of Tarangini Foundation at the field level. The role assists in the planning, execution, monitoring, and documentation of program interventions to ensure the timely achievement of expected results and outcomes.

Under the direct supervision of the Project Coordinator, the Field Officer will regularly conduct field visits, monitor ongoing activities, and provide technical and coordination support to community groups, including Women Human Rights Defenders (WHRDs), youth groups, and other stakeholders.

The role requires close coordination with municipal authorities, local governments, and other local NGOs to strengthen collaboration, ensure coherence, and create an enabling environment for advancing the organization’s mission and program objectives.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Prepare monthly, quarterly, and yearly plans and ensure effective implementation of field-level activities in alignment with organizational goals and approved work plans.
  • Work closely with Elected Women Representatives, communities, WHRDs, informal workers’ networks, youth groups, municipal authorities and local governments.
  • Represent Tarangini Foundation in local-level events, meetings, and programs, and build strong relationships with local NGOs and community groups.
  • Facilitate joint monitoring visits, track field-level progress, identify gaps, support corrective actions, and document key achievements and lessons learned.
  • Prepare and submit high-quality monthly, quarterly, and annual reports.
  • Ensure proper documentation of expenses, adherence to financial procedures, and compliance with organizational policies, promoting accountability, transparency, and safeguarding practices.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in social sciences, Development Studies, or any relevant field.
  • At least 1–2 years of relevant field-level experience, preferably in community-based or rights-based programs.
  • Strong understanding of gender justice, women’s rights, feminist approaches, and community mobilization.
  • Experience working with Women Human Rights Defenders (WHRDs), youth groups, women’s groups, or other community-based structures will be an asset.
  • Excellent communication, coordination, interpersonal, and relationship-building skills, with a strong commitment to feminist and rights-based approaches.
  • Willingness and ability to travel extensively across Morang, Sunsari, and Udayapur as required by the position.
  • Proficiency in MS Office applications, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.

Application Procedure:

Tarangini Foundation values diversity and strongly encourages women, Dalit/Janajati, and candidates from sexual minority communities to apply.

Qualified candidates are requested to submit their cover letter, detailing their experience and motivation for the position, along with an updated CV to documentation@tarangini.org.np with the subject line: “Field Officer” by 20-September-2026. The application will be evaluated on a rolling basis.

Applications without a cover letter and CV will not be considered. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for a written test and interview. No telephone inquiries will be entertained.

Tarangini Foundation reserves the right to modify, postpone, or cancel the recruitment process, or to make no appointment, if deemed necessary.

Position: Logistics Officer
Opening: 1 position
Location: Rasuwa
Duration: 1 September 2026 to 28 February 2028
Reports to: Finance and Logistics Coordinator

Introduction

People in Need (PIN) is a non-governmental, non-profit, international organisation founded in the Czech 1992. PIN arrived in Nepal as part of a humanitarian response to the April 25, 2015 earthquake. Since its inception in Nepal, PIN has had a strong role in designing and facilitating systemic solutions, advocating for and addressing the needs of vulnerable populations affected by disasters, including person categories who live in geographically remote areas of the country, historically marginalised ethnic groups, and those marginalised because of their age and/or gender identity. Currently, PIN Nepal is implementing programmes under three strategic pillars: 1) Emergency response and recovery, 2) Climate resilience, and 3) Civil society and inclusive governance. PIN Nepal team works in and promotes strong partnerships with civil society, the Government of Nepal, academia, the private sector and other key stakeholders in Nepal. Together with them, PIN Nepal has become one of the pioneer organisations advancing programmes such as landslide disaster preparedness and anticipatory action, climate and flood resilient housing, durable local solutions, climate change modelling for more inclusive and efficient local decision-making, girls and inclusive education, waste management and circular economy approaches. PIN is strongly committed to safeguarding children and vulnerable adults, including persons with disabilities, in line with its safeguarding framework and child protection policy.

Scope of Work

The Logistics Officer is responsible for ensuring timely, efficient, and accountable logistics support for emergency flood response operations. The position will oversee procurement, transportation, warehousing, asset management, fleet coordination, and distribution of relief supplies to affected communities while ensuring compliance with organizational policies, donor requirements, and humanitarian standards.

All PIN staff agree to:

  • Comply with all relevant PIN policies, Country Program Policies, and guidelines related to their position.
  • Show a strong commitment to the inclusion of all groups within Nepal and dedication to PIN Nepal’s Inclusion Guidelines.
  • Perform and accurately complete administrative tasks related to their position.
  • Strive for quality in all aspects of their work and ensure the highest quality performance of the Country Program.
  • Maintain a positive attitude and promote a professional & productive working environment across all staff, departments, and among all of PIN’s partners.
  • Adhere to PIN Code of Conduct and key policies including Anti-Corruption Policy, Child Protection Policy and Safeguarding Policy.

About the Project

People in Need (PIN) is implementing an Emergency Flood Response Project in Rasuwa District to provide timely humanitarian assistance to flood-affected communities. The project focuses on addressing immediate humanitarian needs through emergency relief, early recovery support, and the restoration of essential services while ensuring accountability, compliance, and efficient use of resources.

Efficient logistics and supply chain management are critical to the success of the response. The project therefore requires robust procurement, warehousing, transportation, fleet management, and distribution systems to ensure that relief items and resources are delivered safely, timely, and in compliance with donor, organisational, and humanitarian standards.

The Logistics Officer will play a key role in supporting emergency operations by ensuring the effective management of procurement processes, inventory control, transportation, asset management, and supply chain activities to facilitate the successful implementation of the Emergency Flood Response Project across Rasuwa District.

Key Summary of Functions

The Logistics Officer is responsible for managing the end-to-end logistics function for emergency flood response operations, including the procurement, transportation, storage, and distribution of relief supplies. The role ensures effective warehouse and inventory management through regular stock monitoring, accurate record-keeping, and proper control of relief items. The position coordinates fleet operations, vehicle maintenance, and transportation arrangements to support timely delivery of assistance. The Logistics Officer supports procurement processes and supplier management in compliance with organisational policies and donor requirements, while facilitating accountable and efficient distribution of relief items to flood-affected communities. The role also maintains comprehensive logistics documentation and reporting systems, coordinates closely with program teams, suppliers, local authorities, and other stakeholders, and monitors logistics activities to identify and address risks or operational bottlenecks. Additionally, the Logistics Officer ensures adherence to humanitarian principles, safeguarding standards, and organisational procedures, while providing rapid and flexible logistical support during emergency response deployments.

Requirements

Logistics and Supply Chain Management

  • Coordinate the procurement, transportation, storage, and distribution of emergency relief items.
  • Ensure uninterrupted supply of essential materials required for flood response activities.
  • Monitor stock levels and maintain accurate inventory records.
  • Support rapid mobilisation and delivery of humanitarian assistance to targeted communities.
  • Coordinate with program teams to forecast logistics needs and replenishment requirements.

Warehouse and Inventory Management

  • Manage warehouse operations and ensure safe storage of relief supplies.
  • Maintain stock cards, inventory registers, and warehouse documentation.
  • Conduct regular physical stock counts and reconcile discrepancies.
  • Ensure proper handling, labeling, and tracking of all inventory items.
  • Implement inventory control measures to minimize losses and damages.

Transportation and Fleet Management

  • Coordinate transportation of relief materials, equipment, and personnel.
  • Monitor vehicle utilisation, maintenance schedules, and fuel consumption.
  • Ensure compliance with vehicle safety and security standards.
  • Maintain fleet records, movement logs, and transport documentation.
  • Support transportation planning for emergency distributions and field visits.

Procurement Support

  • Support procurement activities in line with organisational and donor policies.
  • Prepare logistics specifications and procurement documentation.
  • Assist in obtaining quotations and evaluating suppliers.
  • Follow up with suppliers to ensure timely delivery of goods and services.
  • Maintain procurement and logistics records for audit purposes.

Distribution and Emergency Response Support

  • Facilitate distribution of relief items to flood-affected populations.
  • Support beneficiary verification and distribution planning.
  • Ensure proper documentation of distributions, including distribution reports and beneficiary records.
  • Monitor distribution activities to ensure transparency and accountability.
  • Participate in rapid response deployments as required.

Compliance, Reporting, and Documentation

  • Ensure logistics operations comply with organisational policies and donor requirements.
  • Prepare weekly and monthly logistics reports.
  • Maintain organised filing systems for logistics documentation.
  • Support internal and external audits by providing required records.
  • Report logistics challenges, risks, and mitigation measures to management.

Coordination and Communication

  • Coordinate with program, finance, administration, and field teams.
  • Liaise with suppliers, transporters, local authorities, and other stakeholders as required.
  • Participate in coordination meetings and emergency response planning sessions.
  • Support community engagement efforts related to logistics and distributions.

Requirements

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Logistics, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Management, or a related field.

Experience

  • Minimum 2 years of relevant experience in logistics, procurement, supply chain, or humanitarian operations.
  • Experience supporting emergency response, disaster management, or flood response programs preferred.
  • Experience in warehouse and fleet management.
  • Experience working with NGOs, INGOs, or humanitarian agencies is desirable.

Required Competencies

  • Knowledge of logistics and supply chain management principles.
  • Inventory and warehouse management skills.
  • Fleet and transportation management.
  • Procurement and vendor management.
  • Reporting and documentation skills.
  • Strong planning and organisational skills.
  • Ability to work under pressure and meet tight deadlines.
  • Problem-solving and decision-making skills.
  • High level of integrity and accountability.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
  • Ability to work effectively in emergency and field-based environments.
  • Fluency in Nepali and good written and spoken English.

Additional Requirements

  • Willingness to travel extensively to flood-affected areas.
  • Ability to work beyond normal office hours during emergency operations.
  • Commitment to humanitarian principles, safeguarding, and protection standards.

Note: The position requires flexibility and rapid deployment to support emergency flood response activities as required by the project.

Posiiton: Emergency Response Manager

The Organisation

Plan International is an independent development and humanitarian organisation that advances children’s rights and equality for girls. We believe in the power and potential of every child but know this is often suppressed by poverty, violence, exclusion and discrimination. And it is girls who are most affected.

Working together with children, young people, supporters and partners, we strive for a just world, tackling the root causes of the challenges girls and vulnerable children face. We support children’s rights from birth until they reach adulthood and we enable children to prepare for and respond to crises and adversity. We drive changes in practice and policy at local, national and global levels using our reach, experience and knowledge.

For over 85 years, we have rallied other determined optimists to transform the lives of all children in more than 80 countries.

We won’t stop until we are all equal.

ROLE PURPOSE

Plan International is responding to the Nepal Flash Floods August 2026 crisis in Nepal through a multi-sector and multi-donor funded program. We are recruiting an Emergency Response Manager to oversee and lead that program delivery.

Plan International Nepal’s country strategy is designed to address the specific needs of girls, boys, women and men affected by disasters putting special emphasis on gender equality in a way that it contributes to the resilience of the communities in a long run. Plan International Nepal is currently responding to the ongoing flash floods in Nepal, with a focus on addressing the immediate humanitarian needs of the most vulnerable and at-risk populations. The response aims to reduce the impacts of the disaster, protect the health, safety, and well-being of affected communities, and prevent further harm, particularly among girls, women, children, and children and adults with disabilities. The intervention also seeks to strengthen protection, access to essential services, and community resilience while mitigating the longer-term social and economic consequences of the flash floods.

The Emergency Response Manager (ERM) will be responsible for working closely with Technical Advisors, support departments and implementing partners as a strategic and technical guide to ensure quality assurance of project interventions, as well as meeting the compliance requirements of donors and Plan International.

S/He will be fully responsible for the overall implementation, coordination and reporting of the Nepal Flash Floods August 2026 ensuring the quality and timely delivery of the project activities maintaining highest technical quality according to the objectives and approach in the project document, fund agreement document and to the satisfaction of project stakeholders. S/he will be accountable for the quality implementation of the above in alignment with Plan’s global strategies/standards and Country Strategy. S/He will technically lead implementation of all projects including planning, M&E, financial management, procurement and knowledge management in close guidance of the Director of program delivery.

S/he is responsible to achieve a rights-based, gender transformative and inclusive program. S/He will also support on influence work approach in program implementation, ensuring efficient technical support to partner NGOs.

Dimensions of the Role

The ERM will be the lead of Nepal Flash Flood August 2026 response team. S/he will be a budget holder and have to monitor and manage the budget under her/his portfolio. The position works in close coordination and support of the Cash focal person, Protection Technical Advisor, Senior Technical Advisor-WASH, the Gender Technical Advisor and other relevant sectoral leads. The position will work with the Grants and Compliance Manager to ensure that the reporting requirements have been met timely and the proper external communication have been done. This is a managerial position responsible for ensuring the implementation of the ERP.

Internal and External interfaces:

Accountabilities

Functional Competencies

Design and Develop strategy/framework

  • Ensure all the projects under emergency response program are gender aware and those longer than 6 months are gender transformative and inclusive
  • Ensure the proper context specific adoptive management during emergency response planning for the anticipated potential external factor such as; monsoon floods, landslides, water borne diseases etc.
  • Ensure that the emergency response projects contributes towards community resilience
  • Ensure that the emergency response program adhere to the country strategy, cluster standards, humanitarian principles and standards, DRRM policies and strategic action plan.
  • Ensure that the Nepal Flash Flood recovery plan revised/updated to address the changing vulnerabilities and the context incorporating the learnings from ongoing response.
  • Incorporate innovation and new ways of creating positive change for children and young people through program and influencing; and
  • Identify, develop and disseminate tools, guidelines and standards for the implementation of effective emergency response work within the organization.

Project Management

  • Prepare Detail Implementation Plan (DIP) and Project Outlines (POs) and provide technical backstopping to project implementing partner(s) in line with approved DIP and PO. Develop a realistic, prioritized, result-based budget plan & budget forecast.
  • Review Partners proposal/ provide feedback and correction as needed
  • Review the projects periodically and ensure project objectives are achieved effectively.
  • Review project documents and progress report to ensure activities carried out are of quality and implemented punctually.
  • Identify risks and challenges in the project implementation, management and provide solution to achieve project goal / results.
  • Identify the training needs/gap of the plan and partner staff and provide/recommend training plans to develop their technical expertise.
  • Knowledge management through, sharing good practice, lessons learned
  • Conduct regular reviews of budgets and work plans to ensure compliance with donor specific requirements and address any changes to the original plan in time.
  • Develop and submit reports on time as outlined in the project agreement
  • Work with MER team to ensure that the CEA component well integrated in the emergency response program implementation.
  • Develop SOP for partner and ensure that SOPs are followed and compliances are maintained at Plan and the partners following no-harm principles.
  • A risk matrix is developed for both and partner and mitigation measures are in place; the risk matrix is periodically reviewed.

Monitoring and supervision

  • Ensure an approved M&E framework and relevant tools are in place and shared with the project staff members for utilisation.
  • Ensure that partner staff members are oriented on the project’s M&E framework and adapted for monitoring and progress tracking of interventions.
  • Ensure effective project monitoring by taking necessary corrective actions that are being followed up and reviewed periodically
  • Undertake field monitoring visits (desktop monitoring in case of movement restriction) and report performance against established schedules and targets
  • Review the data/information provided by Monitoring, Evaluation and Research (MER) specialist, provide input and make effective monitoring plan.
  • Work closely with the MER team at Country Office to ensure that implementation of the activities is done in line with M&E requirements. This include ensuring that links exist with reporting requirements, data management, documentation of best practices, case studies and learning and as set out in plan/log frame.

Resource Mobilisation

  • Work in collaboration with the Business Development Team and NO on proposal design and budget allocation.

Working in Partnership

  • Provide technical support and feedback to program staff both at CO and field, CBO, NGOs, R/Municipality and other concerned individuals to ensure quality design, accountability and implementation of the project activities.

Advocacy & Influencing

title.rendered: Supply chain, Admin and Safety Security Coordinator

content.rendered:
Save the Children believes every child deserves a future. In Bhutan and around the world, we give children a healthy start in life, the opportunity to learn and protection from harm. We do whatever it takes for children – every day and in times of crisis – transforming their lives and future we share. Save the Children expects that anyone associated with it abides by its Safeguarding and other Zero Tolerance Policies.

Reference Check will be done for all candidates- so the application to include reference details. The selected candidate needs to be ready to join within 24 hours of offer.

Position: Supply chain, Admin and Safety Security Coordinator
TEAM/PROGRAMME: Supply Chain
LOCATION: Nuwakot
GRADE: 3
POST TYPE: National (6 months) Possible of extension

Child Safeguarding:

Level 2: either the post holder will have access to personal data about children and/or young people as part of their work; or the post holder will be working in a ‘regulated’ position (accountant, barrister, solicitor, legal executive); therefore, a police check will be required (at ‘standard’ level in the UK or equivalent in other countries).

ROLE PURPOSE:

The Supply chain, Admin and Safety Security Coordinator is responsible for setting up effective & efficient Supply chain management system and lead the Field office Supply chain unit. The position will be the lead in setting up sourcing strategy, sourcing pipeline, tracking, and monitoring performance indicator of sourcing function, establish contracts and Framework Agreements with the suppliers, warehouse and distribution, fleet management as well as admin and safety and security management for the Field office.

The position will be responsible for the preparation of procurement plan, execution of procurement process, timely delivery of goods and services, providing support on procurement to partners. This role also provides technical support, capacity building and will be responsible for ensuring sound logistics practices and rigorous controls are in place for the support of all programs and partners.

SCOPE OF ROLE:

Reports to: Field Operations Lead

Staff Reporting to this post:

Direct reporting: Guard; Support Staff, and Drivers

Indirect reporting:

Budget responsibilities:

Role Dimensions: This position will be fully responsible for managing and leading supply chain and admin function of field office and also ensure the safety security of staff, assets and programs. The position is required to work and coordinate closely with the CO supply chain Unit, Budget Holders, Program Managers/Coordinators, other relevant departments in Field Offices, other stake holder from Finance, HR, Media & Communication, Supply Chain team and various service providers or suppliers.

KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY:

Technical/Functional responsibility

  • Lead and manage the overall supply chain management of field Office.
  • Manage and take leadership for complex and high value sourcing process (Formal and tender threshold) ​
  • Responsible for performance management of the supply chain function of field office through improved KPI and take initiatives to improve efficiency and effectiveness of the procurement function.
  • Ensure an internal review and validation mechanism is in place for procurement processes in field office to strengthen compliance and reduce risks for the organization.
  • Lead on development consolidation of Sourcing Pipelines for field office and track/monitor sourcing pipeline on quarterly basis and advise procurement coordinator.
  • Lead and manage on establishing Contract / FWA/ LTA as per the sourcing pipeline and regular track and monitor contract /FWA.
  • Take lead on measuring and reporting financial benefits and prepare BAF.
  • Take lead for running tenders and submit to CO with relevant documentation for review and validation – when required by the threshold.
  • Ensure roles and responsibilities of procurement committee members are known and people adhere to it.
  • Review procurement waivers and ensure that they are compliant prior to submitting to the required person for approval.
  • Ensure qualified vendor are updated following the due diligence evaluation and the Suppliers management process is updated on Ariba network in regular basis.
  • Conduct periodic visit to all the partners, monitor and assess the partners capacity in regards of supply chain management and coach and support partners supply chain staffs for the smooth supply chain process.
  • Make sure warehouses are managed adequately for various program supplies including incoming of goods, safeguarding of goods, outgoing and distribution of supplies and equipment’s for program following the SCI standard system.
  • Monitor proper utilization of program supplies, report concern Field Operations Lead and Budget Holder regarding non-utilization of supplies.
  • Ensure the mode of transports are cost efficient and preparedness plan for the response is updated.
  • Coordinate with relevant budget holders for the replenishment and utilization of preposition stocks are in line.
  • Establish right size of fleet and make efficient and cost effectiveness as per context and current guidelines.
  • Analysis the fleet tracker and make sure availability and utilization is on track.
  • Ensure smooth admin and office operational strategy.
  • Work as security focal person of the field office and update regular security report to Field Operations Lead, Safety and Security Manager in Country Office.
  • Work closely with Safety and security manager to ensure all safety and security measures are in place, updated and informed to all field office staff.
  • Conduct safety and security assessment in regular basis and issue advisory with close coordination with Safety and Security manager.
  • Analysis the Field office risk matrix and implement mitigation measures in coordination with Risk owners.
  • Conduct awareness orientation to SCI staffs and Partners staffs in regards of safety and security.
  • Maintain the good coordination with government lines securities agency and other stake holders.
  • To adhere Safeguarding Policy, to appropriately safeguard child and adult beneficiaries and support the Program as per the role.
  • Organise and facilitate regular knowledge sharing sessions for the procurement and supply chain team members in field office.
  • Prepare capacity development plan for partners staffs and execute on time.

Coordination and collaboration

  • Work effectively with stakeholders at various internal and external level.
  • Closely work with Program, Finance, Award and other relevant Department on review and tracking for procurement plans/sourcing pipeline, BvA review, charging, recharging, closing, and various other issues when necessary.
  • Closely work with Awards/program team and provide inputs for new proposal development, donor reporting and compliance issues. Participate in kick off meetings.
  • Work with internal and external audit teams and provide necessary requisites.
  • Work closely with Sr supply chain and Admin manager, Safety and security manager, HR manager and IT manager at CO.

Counter Fraud and Safeguarding Responsibilities:

  • Take all necessary and appropriate steps to prevent abuse, exploitation, neglect, harm and modern slavery within their areas of responsibility, and in the way they conduct themselves, report and respond to all incidents and concerns whether online or in person, and comply with the Safeguarding Policy and Procedure.
  • Take all necessary and appropriate steps to prevent fraud, bribery, and corruption within their areas of responsibility, report and respond to all incidents and concerns and comply with the Counter-Fraud, Bribery and Corruption Policy and Procedure. All types of fraud, bribery, and corruption must be prevented, including where it benefits the organisation (SCI).

SKILLS AND BEHAVIOURS (our Values in Practice)

Accountability:

  • Holds self-accountable for making decisions, managing resources efficiently, achieving and role modelling Save the Children values
  • Holds the team and partners accountable to deliver on their responsibilities – giving them the freedom to deliver in the best way they see fit, providing the necessary development to improve performance and applying appropriate consequences when results are not achieved.
  • Sets ambitious and challenging goals for themselves and their team, takes responsibility for their own personal development and encourages others to do the same.
  • Widely shares their personal vision for Save the Children, engages and motivates others.
  • Future orientated, thinks strategically.
  • Builds and maintains effective relationships, with their team, colleagues, Members and external partners and supporters.
  • Values diversity sees it as a source of competitive strength.
  • Approachable, good listener, easy to talk to
  • Develops and encourages new and innovative solutions.
  • Willing to take disciplined risks.
  • Honest, encourages openness and transparency

Ambition:

Collaboration:

Creativity:

Integrity:

QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

  • Master’s degree in business management, social science or relevant areas/or equivalent with minimum 4 years (3 years for GSI group) of working experience in procurement field OR bachelor’s degree in business management, social science or relevant areas with 6 years (4 years for GSI group) of experience procurement field.
  • Prior experience in the I/NGO sector in procurement and admin function
  • Representation and negotiation skill
  • Skills in organising programs, coordination, and documentation,
  • Strong personal organizational skills, including time management, Analytical skills, and ability to meet deadlines and work under pressure.
  • Willingness to work the time necessary to complete critical tasks without being asked.
  • Good written and spoken English.
  • High level of computer skills
  • Cultural awareness and ability to work well in multicultural environment with people from diverse backgrounds and cultures.
  • Commitment to Save the Children’s values, vision and mission.

EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS

Equal Opportunities:

The role holder is required to carry out the duties in accordance with the SCI Equal Opportunities and Diversity policies and procedures.

Safeguarding obligation:

We need to keep children, adult at risk and community safe. The position holder is responsible to ensure that The position holder conduct is in line with the SCI’s Safeguarding policies. Hence our selection process includes rigorous background checks, reflects our commitment to the protection of children, adult at risk and community from abuse, exploitation, and harassment.

Health and Safety:

The role holder is required to carry out the duties in accordance with SCI Health and Safety policies and procedures.

Safeguarding our Staff:

The post holder is required to carry out the duties in accordance with the SCI anti-harassment policy.

Counter Fraud

The role holder is required to take all necessary and appropriate steps to prevent fraud, bribery, and corruption within their areas of responsibility, report and respond to all incidents and concerns and comply with the Counter-Fraud, Bribery and Corruption Policy and Procedure. All types of fraud, bribery, and corruption must be prevented, including where it benefits the organisation (SCI).

The Organisation

We employ approximately 25,000 people across the globe and work on the ground in over 100 countries to help children affected by crises, or those that need better healthcare, education and child protection. We also campaign and advocate at the highest levels to realise the right of children and to ensure their voices are heard.

We are working towards three breakthroughs in how the world treats children by 2030:

  • No child dies from preventable causes before their 5th birthday
  • All children learn from a quality basic education and that,
  • Violence against children is no longer tolerated

We know that great people make a great organization, and that our employees play a crucial role in helping us achieve our ambitions for children. We value our people and offer a meaningful and rewarding career, along with a collaborative and inclusive workplace where ambition, creativity, and integrity are highly valued.

Application Information

Please apply using a cover letter and up-to-date CV as a single document. Please also include details of your current remuneration and salary expectations.

We need to keep children safe so our selection process, which includes rigorous background checks, reflects our commitment to the protection of children from abuse.

All employees are expected to carry out their duties in accordance with our global anti-harassment policy.

Save the Children does not charge a fee at any stage of the recruitment process.

CALL FOR CONSULTANCY PROPOSAL
Hiring of Technical Consultant/Resource Person (RP)
Organization: Social Network for Justice & Development (SN-JD)
Location: Jhapa, Koshi Province, Nepal
Assignment: Design, Facilitation and Documentation of Two-Day Tabletop Exercise (TTX)
Working Area: Shivasatakshi Municipality, Jhapa
Implementation Partner: Shivasatakshi Municipality

About the Assignment
Social Network for Justice & Development (SN-JD), in partnership with Shivasatakshi Municipality, invites applications from qualified and experienced individual consultants or consulting teams for the design, facilitation and documentation of a two-day Tabletop Exercise (TTX) on Monsoon Flood and Inundation Preparedness, Response and Early Recovery.

The exercise will focus on testing municipal preparedness, early warning and decision-making, information flow, coordination, evacuation, search and rescue, emergency shelter, food, WASH, health, protection, education, resource mobilization and early recovery mechanisms.

Key Responsibilities
The selected Consultant/RP will:

  • Review the Municipality’s Monsoon Preparedness and Response Action Plan, 2083 and relevant DRM frameworks.
  • Develop a realistic flood/inundation scenario, injects, role cards, discussion questions and evaluation tools.
  • Design and facilitate the two-day TTX/simulation involving approximately 40–50 participants.
    Facilitate coordination and decision-making among municipality, wards, security agencies, LEOC and other stakeholders.
  • Integrate GEDSI and protection considerations into the exercise.
  • Facilitate an After Action Review and identify key gaps, lessons learned and priority actions.
  • Prepare and submit a concise final TTX report with recommendations.

Required Qualification and Experience

  • At least a Bachelor’s degree in Disaster Risk Management/Disaster Management, Development Studies, Rural Development, Social Sciences, Emergency Management or a relevant field; Master’s degree will be an advantage.
  • At least 5 years of relevant professional experience in DRR/DRM, emergency preparedness and response, humanitarian programming or related areas.
  • Demonstrated experience in designing/facilitating TTX, simulation exercises, mock drills or similar preparedness exercises.
  • Good understanding of Nepal’s disaster risk management system and local government disaster preparedness and response mechanisms.
  • Experience working with local governments, LEOCs, security agencies, NGOs/CBOs and/or humanitarian/development partners.
  • Strong facilitation, communication, coordination and report-writing skills.
    Knowledge and experience in GEDSI/inclusive disaster risk management will be an advantage.

Application Requirements
Interested consultants/consulting teams are requested to submit:

  • Updated CV/Profile;
  • Brief technical proposal/methodology;
  • Proposed work plan and timeline;
  • Evidence/list of similar assignments;
  • At least two relevant references; and
  • Financial proposal with professional fee and applicable taxes/costs.

Submission

Interested applicants may submit proposals via:

Email: procurement.snjd@gmail.com
Or: Hard copy at SN-JD Contact Office, Birtamode, Jhapa

Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted. SN-JD reserves the right to accept or reject any or all proposals without assigning any reason.

For detailed Terms of Reference (ToR), Visit: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1VOcvwVskg9wbbNEqJQDb1lO07J0Xo6qr/edit?pli=1
Or contact SN-JD or request the ToR by email.

Position: Sustainable Infrastructure Specialist
Location: Kathmandu

Company Description

WWF Nepal, the global conservation organization leading international efforts for a living planet, seeks applications from qualified Nepali candidates for the following full-time position. If you think you are an achiever and willing to work within a diverse team in a multicultural environment with commitment and passion for what you believe in, you are highly encouraged to apply.

Our Mission

At WWF Nepal, we firmly believe people and nature are inextricably linked. Our mission is to stop the degradation of our planet’s natural environment and build a future Nepal in which people live in harmony with nature.

Our Vision

From its origins as a small group of committed wildlife enthusiasts, WWF has grown into one of the world’s largest and most respected independent conservation organizations, active in over 100 countries.

Over this time, WWF’s focus has evolved from localized efforts in favor of a single species and individual habitats to an ambitious strategy to preserve biodiversity and achieve sustainable development across the globe.

WWF-Nepal envisions a prosperous Nepal, with an active and socially responsible citizenry that a greater sense of stewardship towards the environment.

Our Core Values

We celebrate and respect diversity in nature and among the people, partners, and communities with whom we work. Across the many cultures and individuals that represent WWF, we are unified by one mission, one brand, and one common set of values:

Courage: We demonstrate courage through our actions, we work for change where it’s needed, and we inspire people and institutions to tackle the greatest threats to nature and the future of the planet, which is our home.

Integrity: We live the principles we call on others to meet. We act with integrity, accountability, and transparency, and we rely on facts and science to guide us and to ensure we learn and evolve.

Respect: We honor the voices and knowledge of the people and communities that we serve, and we work to secure their rights to a sustainable future.

Collaboration: We deliver impact at the scale of the challenges we face through the power of collective action and innovation.

Job Description

Major Functions:

The Sustainable Infrastructure Specialist will be responsible for assessing the potential impacts of large-scale infrastructure on conservation and developing strategic, collaborative approaches to address the issue in an amicable manner. Under the supervision of the Conservation Program Director, the Specialist will be responsible for building and strengthening the capacity of government agencies, civil society organizations, development partners, and academic institutions while coordinating closely with relevant stakeholders to promote sustainable green infrastructure (wildlife-friendly and climate-smart) to reduce any adverse impacts of infrastructure on the ecosystem and biodiversity.

Major Duties and Responsibilities:

1. Technical support to appraise and address the adverse impacts of infrastructure development

Working closely with the supervisor, as well as internal and external stakeholders at both field and central levels, the incumbent will support work on sustainable green infrastructure—both broadly and within WWF’s priority landscapes—to assess and, where possible, mitigate the adverse impacts of infrastructure (primarily linear and point) development on biodiversity, including wildlife, freshwater systems, and forests. Key responsibilities include, but are not limited to: identifying and mapping planned infrastructure developments across landscapes; reviewing environmental and social impacts, including those arising from unsustainable extraction of construction materials; assessing and providing inputs on developers’ Environmental Impact Assessments (EIA/IEE); identifying cumulative impacts of multiple infrastructure projects and preparing case studies and analytical reports grounded in data and evidence; coordinating stakeholder identification and engagement in the environmental flows (E-flows) process; and identifying best practices and recommending appropriate mitigation measures for the planning, design, and implementation of major linear and point infrastructure projects. The role is expected to focus primarily on hydropower development, transmission lines, new roads and railway lines, highway expansions, irrigation systems, urban growth, and other emerging infrastructure priorities.

2. Provide technical support in Green recovery and mainstreaming Climate Change and DRR in infrastructure work

Work closely with WWF core team, disaster relief committees, donors, and other networks; promote awareness, provide technical advice, and develop a strategy for Green recovery and reconstruction, identifying priority needs and opportunities based on needs using WWF’s existing experience and knowledge. The incumbent works closely with the Climate and Energy thematic team, promotes mainstreaming of climate adaptation and Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) into the infrastructure sector, identify measures together with developers and donors to take account of possible risks from climate and development scenarios. Support building climate resilient and carbon neutral infrastructure through designing and implementation of practices, protocols, and guidelines.

3. Technical Suggestion to senior leadership team and Cross Learning among WWF’s Thematic Teams

Proactively update WWF Nepal’s senior management team and thematic leads on major infrastructure developments, as well as relevant laws, policies, and emerging environmental risks associated with development activities, to help shape and position WWF Nepal’s response. This includes regularly monitoring key projects, synthesizing complex information, and delivering timely analyses supported by accurate data, verified evidence, geospatial insights, and illustrative case studies to inform strategic decision-making and programmatic actions.

4. Coordinate with donors, developers, academics, and government to strengthen the enabling environment and best practices

Develop working relationships with developers, donors, and relevant government departments, local and state governments to enhance the enabling environment and best practices in environmentally friendly infrastructure development. Provide inputs in policies (drafting and revision) related to infrastructure development and natural resources safeguards. This responsibility may include coordination with different CSO/Network/interest groups that are actively engaged in any infrastructure development project in the country. Coordinate with academia (School, Campus and university) to support mainstreaming infrastructure issues in their curricula.

5. Support the development team and field team in the design and implementation of safeguard measures in related projects

Work as focal point for nature safeguarding of all infrastructure related works as demanded by infrastructure related projects. The incumbent will work closely with WWF’s development team towards the inception of new concept notes and design of projects relevance to WWF’s infrastructure work. Specialists shall contribute towards other thematic teams in developing integrated projects in WWF’s working landscape. For assigned projects, provide technical guidance for implementation to the field team, researcher/consultants and contribute to project completion reports and address relevant thematic areas as required by the project deliverables. Keep track of issues or related developments that are useful for safeguards implementation and new or updates to country safeguard systems (e.g., laws, policies, regulations, and procedures).

6. Monitoring, Evaluation, Knowledge and Learning

Working closely with Monitoring and Evaluation staff, monitoring progress of the infrastructure work and contributing to performance monitoring, progress reports and final program reports. Enhance knowledge and learning on best practices including Sustainable Green Infrastructure (SGI) practices; document lessons from infrastructure work and contribute to WWF Nepal’s learning program including knowledge sharing and capacity building. The incumbent should keep track of the progress in the field of infrastructure development, including at bilateral and multilateral levels. In addition, s/he should be continuously keeping track of public sector investment by local and state level governments in areas of WWF interest, particularly conservation landscapes and areas of biodiversity significance.

7. Communication and Technical Reporting

Promote communication of messages on infrastructure impacts and ways to reduce them, such as modeling tools for decision makers; awareness and outreach events; and production of publications, technical reports, and other materials; for key audiences including decision makers, developers, donors, practitioners, partners, and the public. FUNCTION

The Financial Inclusion Officer-Financial Inclusion will lead the PROSPER project’s financial inclusion portfolio, providing strategic and technical support to improve farmers’, cooperatives’, and SMEs’ access to appropriate finance, markets, and enterprise-development opportunities.

The role will strengthen stakeholder capacity, facilitate partnerships with financial institutions, fintech/agritech firms, buyers, and investors, support farmer-friendly financing initiatives such as FEBL Lite, oversee loan facilitation and repayment performance, and provide timely analysis and recommendations to the Project Manager and thematic leads.

Financial Inclusion and Technical Assistance (50%)

  • Lead financial, business, and digital literacy initiatives, including FEBL Lite, through Bank Saathis, digital facilitators, and tools such as GeoKrishi Farm.
  • Strengthen cooperatives as inclusive business and financial-service hubs by improving governance, financial management, digital systems, and service delivery.
  • Establish and manage Bank Saathi networks to support farmers with loan applications, credit histories, insurance, repayment planning, and digital financial services.
  • Collaborate with BFIs, fintech firms, and other partners to design, pilot, and scale inclusive credit, insurance, and green-finance products for smallholder farmers, women, youth, persons with disabilities, returnee migrants, and agribusinesses.
  • Support loan documentation, responsible use of finance, repayment monitoring, and the adoption of digital tools that improve transparency and reduce transaction costs.
  • Facilitate enterprise development and market linkages through buyer mapping, business-to-business engagement, aggregation, fair contracts, and investment opportunities.
  • Engage local governments and regulators to promote an inclusive, gender-responsive, and climate-sensitive financial ecosystem.
  • Develop and implement structured training, coaching, and mentoring plans for project staff, partners, cooperatives, Bank Saathis, agribusinesses, and farmers.
  • Strengthen business planning, financial management, marketing, negotiation, investment readiness, and market-linkage capacities.
  • Mentor Bank Saathis and cooperatives to improve financial-service outreach, farmer support, and cooperative–bank relationships.
  • Support cooperatives and enterprises to access productive infrastructure, equipment, finance, and cost-sharing opportunities.
  • Develop practical training materials and tools on financial literacy, enterprise development, value chains, and market access.

Collaboration, Partnership and Resource Leveraging (30%)

  • Coordinate with local governments, Heifer teams, BFIs, MFIs, insurance companies, agri-tech/fintech firms, private sector actors, buyers, investors, and value chain stakeholders.
  • Develop inclusive partnership models such as cooperative-bank partnerships, contract farming, out-grower schemes, joint ventures, buyback guarantees, MoUs, and risk-sharing arrangements.
  • Facilitate exposure visits, networking events, trade fairs, and co-design meetings to promote learning, investment, and inclusive business development.
  • Advocate for farmer-friendly financial systems, simplified documentation, improved trust between farmers and BFIs, and reduced transaction costs.
  • Leverage public, private, and philanthropic resources to support enterprise growth, dairy sector development, and market system strengthening.

Monitoring, Review, Documentation and Reporting (15%)

  • Conduct regular field visits to monitor project progress, financial tool adoption, loan disbursement, utilization, repayment, business growth, and partnership performance.
  • Track income improvement, employment generation, borrower feedback, market deals, bankable business plans, and success stories.
  • Maintain updated records on producers, production, yield, marketable quantities, buyers, cooperatives, financial institution linkages, and training participation.
  • Prepare field visit notes, event reports, monthly progress reports, repayment trend analysis, and recommendations for improvement.
  • Ensure reports include disaggregated participant data, key outcomes, challenges, lessons learned, and follow-up actions for the regional and LAGANI Signature Program through Project Manager.

May perform other job-related duties as assigned (5%)

QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLS

  • Bachelor’s degree in economics, management, agriculture/agribusiness, or a related field with (5) five years of relevant experience; or a master’s degree with (3) three years of experience.
  • Proven experience in financial inclusion, loan and investment facilitation, field-program monitoring, and engagement with financial institutions and private sector actors.
  • Experience in agricultural value chains, market linkages, investment promotion, and agriculture or livestock enterprise development.
  • Experience supporting smallholder farmers, cooperatives, agri-enterprises, or agrifood processors, women, person with disability and youth is an advantage.
  • Strong leadership, stakeholder management, coaching, teamwork, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to work independently, take initiative, and manage diverse teams.
  • Fluency in spoken and written Nepali and English.

ESSENTIAL COMPETENCIES AND TRAITS:

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) and virtual collaboration tools.
  • Demonstrate the ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with professionalism while promoting transparency, ethical decision making, and accountability in all aspects of work.
  • The ability to work effectively and respectfully with people from diverse cultural, social, and professional backgrounds.
  • Strong organizational and time management skills.
  • Willingness to work flexibly and ability to travel extensively to rural and project locations to strengthen the relationship to support partners and ensure effective implementation.
  • Demonstrated commitment to Heifer International’s mission, values, and regenerative, locally led program approach.
  • Sensitivity in working with multiple cultures and beliefs, and gender equity.

National Federation of the Disabled Nepal (NFDN) is seeking a qualified and motivated Project Coordinator-Emergency Response to support emergency humanitarian response and early recovery projects in Nuwakot, Rasuwa, and Dhading, Nepal, with support from CBM Global Disability Inclusion Nepal. The Project Coordinator will play a key role in promoting disability-inclusive humanitarian response and recovery by ensuring that planned project activities are implemented on time, within budget, and to a high standard, in close coordination with consortium and implementing partners.

The position will lead and coordinate consortium teams NDWA and BYAN, oversee project implementation and partnerships, monitor the use of resources and achievement of results, ensure compliance and accountability and coordinate with government authorities, humanitarian actors, development partners, and other relevant stakeholders.

NFDN is seeking a qualified, experienced and motivated Finance Officer to support the financial management of its program operation at various projects. The Finance Officer will be responsible for ensuring sound financial management, accounting, budgeting, financial reporting, compliance, and documentation of the project expenditure in accordance with NFDN policies, donor requirements, applicable laws, and agreements with partners. The position will work closely with the project team, consortium/implementing partners, NFDN Finance and Administration team, and relevant stakeholders to ensure effective and transparent utilization of project resources.

The Finance Officer will be based at NFDN Federal Office, Kathmandu, and will report to the Chief Finance Officer and Admin Manager.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Management and Accounting

  • Ensure proper and timely recording of all project financial transactions in accordance with NFDN’s Financial Management and Accounting policies and procedures.

  • Review payment requests, invoices, bills, advances, settlements, and other financial documents for accuracy, completeness, and compliance.

  • Monitor project cash flow and ensure adequate availability of funds for planned activities.

Budget Management and Monitoring

  • Support preparation of project budgets, budget revisions, cash forecasts, and financial plans.
  • Monitor project expenditure against approved budgets and provide regular budget-versus-actual analysis.
  • Identify budget variances, financial risks, and potential overspending or underspending and promptly inform management and project teams.
  • Support project teams in understanding budget requirements and ensuring efficient utilization of resources.
  • Monitor financial performance of implementing and consortium partners in accordance with partnership agreements.

Financial Reporting and Compliance

  • Prepare timely and accurate monthly, quarterly, donor, and project financial reports as required.
  • Support preparation of financial reports and statements for donors and partners in accordance with their requirements.
  • Ensure compliance with NFDN financial policies, donor rules, project agreements, and applicable Government of Nepal regulations.
  • Ensure that financial documentation is complete, properly filed, and readily available for internal and external audits.
  • Support internal and external audits and ensure timely follow-up of audit recommendations.
  • Ensure compliance with NFDN’s anti-fraud, anti-corruption, safeguarding, PSEAH, and other relevant organizational policies.

  • Support partners to strengthen financial management, internal controls, documentation, and accountability.
  • Conduct or support financial monitoring visits to project locations and partner organizations when required.
  • Coordinate with banks, suppliers, auditors, partners, and relevant authorities on financial matters.

Internal Control and Risk Management

  • Ensure effective internal financial controls are maintained throughout project implementation.
  • Identify financial risks and recommend appropriate mitigation measures.
  • Monitor compliance with procurement and financial procedures.
  • Support prevention and detection of financial irregularities, fraud, misuse of resources, and conflicts of interest.
  • Ensure appropriate segregation of financial responsibilities and authorization controls.

Other Responsibilities

  • Support emergency response teams with rapid financial arrangements when required.
  • Provide financial inputs for project proposals, budgets, concept notes, and reports.
  • Maintain confidentiality and integrity of financial information.
  • Contribute to organizational learning and improvement of financial systems.
  • Perform other finance-related duties assigned by NFDN management.

Eligibility to Apply

Education: At least Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Management, Commerce, or a related field.

Experience

  • Experience in managing donor-funded projects and preparing donor financial reports.
  • Experience in budget preparation, expenditure monitoring, financial analysis, and financial reporting.

Skills and Competencies

  • Ability to review financial documents carefully and identify errors, inconsistencies, and compliance issues.
  • Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities under pressure.
  • Strong coordination and communication skills.
  • Ability to provide financial guidance and support to project teams and partners.

  • Engage with girls and young persons with disabilities, including those at heightened risk, and facilitate access to sRHR information and services, empowerment opportunities, protection mechanisms, and other available services and benefits.
  • Support identification of barriers faced by persons with disabilities in accessing emergency services and facilitate appropriate referrals and linkages with service providers.
  • Conduct or support disability inclusion orientations and awareness sessions for frontline responders, including FCHVs, health service providers, security personnel, local authorities, and other relevant actors.
  • Support walk-through accessibility audits of holding centres, temporary shelters, temporary learning centres, health facilities, and other emergency response sites, and document accessibility gaps and recommendations.
  • Support disability-inclusive communication and information dissemination, ensuring that emergency information and key service messages are accessible to persons with different disabilities.
  • Design and implement social media and digital awareness campaigns on disability-inclusive emergency response, youth participation, sRHR, protection, accessibility, and access to services.
  • Mobilize and engage youth volunteers, youth networks, disability organizations, and other community actors in emergency response-related activities.
  • Support the collection of disability-disaggregated information and community feedback to identify emerging needs, barriers, risks, and gaps in emergency response services.
  • Document good practices, challenges, case stories, lessons learned, and emerging evidence related to disability-inclusive emergency response and youth engagement.
  • Maintain regular communication and coordination with BYAN, NFDN, NDWA, CBM Global, other project partners, local government representatives, frontline responders, and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Ensure that activities are implemented in accordance with approved project plans, safeguarding and PSEAH standards, and relevant organizational policies and procedures.
  • Support monitoring, reporting, documentation, accountability to affected populations, and learning related to project interventions.
  • Undertake other duties relevant to the position as assigned by BYAN management.

Required Qualifications and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Social Sciences, Development Studies, Public Health, Social Work, Disability Studies, or a related field. A Master’s degree will be an advantage.
  • At least 2 years of relevant professional experience in disability inclusion, youth engagement, humanitarian/emergency response, community mobilization, sRHR, protection, or related areas.
  • Demonstrated understanding of disability rights, disability inclusion, and meaningful participation of persons with disabilities.
  • Experience working with young persons with disabilities, girls and women with disabilities, OPDs, youth groups, or community-based organizations will be an advantage.
  • Experience facilitating training and orientation sessions for government officials, frontline service providers, community workers, or other stakeholders.
  • Experience in social media campaigns, digital communication, advocacy, or information dissemination will be an advantage.
  • Knowledge and understanding of sRHR, safeguarding, PSEAH, protection, accessibility, and inclusive emergency response.
  • Strong coordination, communication, facilitation, networking, documentation, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a multi-stakeholder team in challenging and rapidly changing emergency contexts.
    Willingness and ability to undertake frequent field visits to project locations.
  • Proficiency in written and spoken Nepali and English.

    Contract Duration: September 2026 to February 2027, with the possibility of extension subject to project requirements, performance, and availability of funding.

Duties

The position is located in the Library of Congress office, US Embassy Nepal and functions as the designated liaison for the Library of Congress in Nepal. Incumbent is supervised by the Field Director for South Asia posted in US Embassy New Delhi, India.

The incumbent acquires and creates online bibliographic records for publications in all languages and formats published in Nepal for the collections of the Library of Congress in Washington D.C., and for libraries of American and Canadian universities who participate in the South Asia Cooperative Acquisitions Program (SACAP). Posiiton: Emergency Finance Officer
Location: Kathmandu with frequent travel to project working areas
Position Status: Full-time, Contract

About Mercy Corps

Mercy Corps is a leading global organization powered by the belief that a better world is possible. In disaster, in hardship, in more than 40 countries around the world, we partner to put bold solutions into action — helping people triumph over adversity and build stronger communities from within. Now, and for the future.

The Program Summary

On 26 August 2026, a glacier and rockfall avalanche near the Rasuwagadhi border triggered a catastrophic debris-flow flood along the Bhotekoshi–Trishuli corridor, severely affecting Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading, districts. Search and rescue operations led by NDRRMA and other responders are ongoing. The disaster has resulted in significant loss of life, injuries, displacement, and extensive damage to infrastructure and livelihoods. Thousands of affected people are facing critical shortages of shelter, water, food, and sanitation supplies. Mercy Corps Nepal is responding to the disaster supporting the affected families with immediate relief and enabling recovery.

The Position (General Position Summary)

The Emergency Finance Officer is responsible for supporting day to day financial operations of the emergency response project ensuring accuracy, timeliness and compliance with Mercy Corps Nepal policiesand regulatory requirements. This position is responsible for processing payments, managing bank-related activities, maintaining accurate accounting records in the financial system, and supporting month-end reconciliations and work closely with partner organization ensuring financial management of partner organization.

Essential Job Responsibilities
The specific duties and responsibilities of the Emergency Finance Officer include, but are not limited to, the following:

FINANCE MANAGEMENT

  • Manage day to day financial operations of the project ensuring compliance with Mercy Corps Nepal policies and other regulatory requirements.
  • Prepare cash flows, monitor project expenditures, and ensure sufficient liquidity for field operations.
  • Process payments, advances and settlements and maintain accurate accounting records and supporting documentation.
  • Manage bank-related correspondence including signatory updates and other communication.
  • Conduct day-to-day data entries into Accounting Software Navigator, ensuring data accuracy and compliance with applicable policies and guidelines.
  • File all vouchers and supporting documents and support proper maintenance of project-related files archive.
  • Review partner/sub-recipient Fund Transfer requests and reconcile with partner financial reports and Navigator data.
  • Prepare photocopies, scans, and other required supporting documents for monthly reporting packages to HQ Finance.
  • Ensure financial management of partner organization and support on financial management capacity building.

COMPLIANCE AND RISK MANAGEMENT

  • Ensure compliance with donor requirements and organizational policies.
  • Support internal and external audits.

COORDINATION AND REPORTING

  • Conduct regular budget monitoring and provides budget Vs expenses analysis to the emergency response coordinator.
  • Support the Interim Senior Finance and Compliance Coordinator in preparation of financial reports, forecasts, and donor financial documentation.
  • Participate in project planning, coordination meetings and emergency response activities as required.
  • Prepare monthly Cash and Bank Reconciliations and get them approved and filed as required.

SAFEGUARDING RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Actively learns about safeguarding and integrates it into their work, including safeguarding risks and mitigations related to their area of work.
  • Practices the values of Mercy Corps including respecting the dignity and well-being of participants and fellow team members.
  • Encourages openness and communication in their team; encourages team members to submit reports if they have any concerns using reporting mechanisms e.g., Integrity Hotline and other options.

Supervisory Responsibility: N/A

Accountability

Reports Directly To: Interim Senior Finance and Compliance Coordinator

Works Directly With: Emergency Response Coordinator and project technical partner team members as required.

Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders

Mercy Corps team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.

Minimum Qualification & Transferable Skills

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in accounting/ financial management or a relevant business field.
  • Minimum of 3-5 years of relevant experience in finance and accounting. Working experience with I/NGOs is preferred.
  • Knowledge of GoN tax regulations, VAT, and TDS requirements.
  • Demonstrated attention to detail, ability to follow procedures, meet deadlines, and work independently and cooperatively with team members.
  • Proficiency in MS Office programs, particularly Excel and financial/accounting software.
