Position: Emergency Monitoring Evaluation & Learning (MEL) and Communications Officer
Location: Nuwakot, Nepal
Position Status: Full-time, Contract

About Mercy Corps

Mercy Corps is a leading global organization powered by the belief that a better world is possible. In disaster, in hardship, in more than 40 countries around the world, we partner to put bold solutions into action helping people triumph over adversity and build stronger communities from within. Now, and for the future.

The Program Summary

On 26 August 2026, a glacier and rockfall avalanche near the Rasuwagadhi border triggered a catastrophic debris-flow flood along the Bhotekoshi–Trishuli corridor, severely affecting Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading, districts. Search and rescue operations led by NDRRMA and other responders are ongoing. The disaster has resulted in significant loss of life, injuries, displacement, and extensive damage to infrastructure and livelihoods. Thousands of affected people are facing critical shortages of shelter, water, food, and sanitation supplies. Mercy Corps Nepal is responding to the disaster supporting the affected families with immediate relief and enabling recovery.

The Position (General Position Summary)

The MEL and Communication Officer support Mercy Corps Nepal’s Emergency Response Program by ensuring monitoring, evaluation and learning systems meet organizational standards, and that program results, learning and best practices are effectively documented and communicated to internal and external stakeholders. The role works closely with the Emergency Response Coordinator, Country MEL Focal Person, and partner to strengthen data quality, participant tracking, and reporting compliance, while also leading communication and knowledge management functions from donor- and media-facing materials to internal learning platforms in line with Mercy Corps’ branding and quality standards.

Essential Job Responsibilities

The specific duties and responsibilities of the MEL and Communications Officer include, but are not limited to, the following:

ASSESSMENT AND MONITORING

  • Support/lead Rapid Needs Assessments (RNA) and contribute to Multi-Sectoral Needs Assessments (MSNA) to inform targeting and response design.
  • Conduct real-time monitoring of response activities against targets, flagging targeting errors, pipeline breaks, or access gaps for immediate correction.
  • Design and conduct Post-Distribution Monitoring (PDM) for cash and in-kind assistance, verifying timeliness, amounts received, use, and continued relevance of transfer values against market prices.
  • Develop compressed, workable MEL frameworks appropriate to the response timeline, and facilitate After Action Reviews (AARs) to document lessons for subsequent response phases.
  • Ensure Mercy Corps’ MEL minimum standards are rolled out and followed across the project/program.
  • Build project team capacity on MEL systems, tools and standards.
  • Plan and facilitate learning events and support thematic teams in capturing and synthesizing field-level learning.

DATA COLLECTION AND QUALITY

  • Design and deploy lean, digital-where-feasible data collection tools appropriate to the acute response phase.
  • Conduct data quality checks and spot verification to ensure reported figures are accurate and defensible.
  • Apply data protection protocols appropriate to the heightened vulnerability of affected populations, including consent and secure storage of PII.

ACCOUNTABILITY

  • Work closely with Country CARM focal person to establish and manage Community Accountability and Response Mechanism (CARM), ensuring safeguarding and protection concerns are identified and referred immediately.
  • Ensure community feedback reaches decisionmakers and informs response adjustments in real time.

COORDINATION AND REPORTING

  • Contribute to 4W/5W coordination reporting to relevant clusters and government entities to avoid duplication and coverage gaps.
  • Track output indicators against cluster standards and produce timely situation reports and donor updates in required formats and timeline.
  • Support Emergency Response Coordinator to prepare periodic progress updates, reports and stories, in collaboration project team, ensuring government and donor compliance.
  • Review project guidelines, documents and resource materials, and prepare shareable resources aligned with Mercy Corps’ and donors’ branding guidelines.

COMMUNICATION AND KNOWLEDGE MANAGEMENT

  • Develop and implement a communication plan to document and disseminate program processes and results to stakeholders.
  • Prepare clear, concise, and compelling reports, presentations and communication materials, and manage internal and external communication channels.
  • Identify and engage key audiences donors, participants and partners through targeted communication strategies and build media relationships to secure positive coverage.
  • Serve as a technical lead for communication and knowledge management, designing and implementing effective tools and mechanisms with the wider team.
  • Capture and document program learning and best practices and organize best-practice-sharing workshops and knowledge products for internal and external audiences.
  • Ensure all communications, outreach and visibility materials comply with the Mercy Corps Nepal Branding Guideline.
  • Collect, structure and maintain project information including a standard information package for internal, external, government and media audiences, ensuring materials remain current and accessible.

SAFEGUARDING RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Actively learns about safeguarding and integrates it into their work, including safeguarding risks and mitigations related to their area of work.
  • Practices the values of Mercy Corps including respecting the dignity and well-being of participants and fellow team members.
  • Encourages openness and communication in their team; encourages team members to submit reports if they have any concerns using reporting mechanisms e.g., Integrity Hotline and other options.

Supervisory Responsibility : N/A

Accountability

Reports Directly To: Emergency Response Coordinator
Works Directly With: Country MEL focal person, CARM Focal person, and partner’s team members.
Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders

Mercy Corps team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.

Minimum Qualification & Transferable Skills

  • Bachelor’s degree in Development Studies/Management, Mass Communications, or a related discipline; Master’s degree preferred.
  • At least 3–5 years of experience in MEL, communications and/or knowledge management with I/NGOs and/or private sector organizations working in disaster risk management, humanitarian assistance.
    Experience designing and implementing MEL systems, including analyzing and promoting the use of collected data.
  • Demonstrated experience with digital data collection technologies and web-based platforms.
  • Knowledge and practical understanding of accountability, particularly to communities and program participants.
  • Previous experience of building MEL capacity, including developing training tools, training, coaching and mentoring.
  • Communication and knowledge management design and implementation skills.
  • Strong written and oral communication skills in English and Nepali, including report writing, analysis and editing.
  • Strong interpersonal, negotiation and representation skills, demonstrated ability to work effectively across multi-cultural, ethnically diverse teams and stakeholders in sensitive environments.
  • Ability to work in complex environments under tight deadlines and changing donor requirements.
  • Good computer skills, including MS Word, Excel and PowerPoint, and online research/information gathering.
  • Photography and videography skills an added advantage.

Success Factors

A successful candidate will have the ability to live and work closely with a diverse team of individuals in a highly intense and fluid work and security environment with a capacity to spark innovative approaches to programming and inspire groups to collaborate closely to implement high-quality humanitarian programs. S/he will have proven ability to learn quickly, take initiative, and be accountable for results, with an ability and willingness to remain mobile for short-term and/or long-term as necessary within the region, based on programmatic needs. An ability to work independently and as part of a team, with curiosity about and sensitivity to new cultures, a desire and ability to learn and grow, both personally and professionally, and a great sense of humor.

The most successful Mercy Corps team members have a strong commitment to teamwork and accountability, thrive in evolving and changing environments and make effective written and verbal communication a priority in all situations. Mercy Corps Team members represent the agency both during and outside of work hours when deployed in a field posting or on a visit/short-term assignment to a field posting. Team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner and respect local laws, customs and MC’s policies, procedures, and values at all times and in all in-country venues.

Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions

The position is based in Nuwakot, Nepal.

Ongoing Learning

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development.

Team Engagement and Effectiveness

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Mercy Corps is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion or belief, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected under applicable law.

Safeguarding & Ethics

Mercy Corps is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary General and IASC and have signed on to The Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to Mercy Corps Code of Conduct Policies and values at all times. Team members are required to complete mandatory Code of Conduct elearning courses upon hire and on an annual basis.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Mercy Corps Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@mercycorps.org).

Position: Operations and Compliance Analyst, Kathmandu, Nepal, NO-A
Job Identification: 36734
Apply Before: 09/30/2026, 11:59 PM
Job Schedule: Full time
Location: Kathmandu, Nepal
Grade: NOA
Vacancy Type: Fixed Term
Rotational/Non Rotational: Non-Rotational
Contract Duration: 1 Year with Possibility for extension
Required Languages: Fluency in oral and written English and national language of the duty station.

Job Description

The Position:

The Operations and Compliance Analyst provides support on financial management, assurance activities, and financial reporting and will provide dedicated operational support to facilitate the implementation and delivery of projects. The Position provides guidance, technical support, and oversight ensuring that resources are utilized appropriately and in compliance with relevant policies and requirements.

The selected candidate will be based at the UNFPA country office, Kathmandu, and will work under the guidance and direct supervision of the International Operations Manager. The Operations and Compliance Analyst will work closely with and will support UNFPA programme officers and the operations team, to ensure major risks and compliance are managed appropriately and programmes are implemented effectively.

How you can make a difference:

UNFPA is the lead United Nations agency for delivering a world where every pregnancy is intended, every childbirth is safe, and every young person’s potential is fulfilled. The UNFPA Strategic Plan for 2026-2029 articulates the organization’s response to a complex global environment, providing a roadmap for resilience and renewal. It is designed to accelerate the implementation of the Programme of Action of the International Conference on Population and Development (ICPD) and the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals by 2030. This mandate is pursued through a focus on four interconnected outcomes: ending the unmet need for family planning; ending preventable maternal deaths; ending gender-based violence and harmful practices; and adapting to demographic change through evidence and rights-based policies.

In a world where fundamental human rights are at risk, we need principled and ethical staff who embody these international norms and standards and will defend them courageously and with full conviction.

UNFPA is seeking candidates who transform, inspire, and deliver high-impact sustained results, ensuring effective external relations, communications, partnership-building and resource mobilization in a rapidly changing development and funding landscape. We need staff who are transparent, exceptional in how they manage the resources entrusted to them, and who commit to delivering excellence in programme results

Job Purpose:

The position will play a supportive role for smooth running of financial, internal control, assurance, oversight, and audit functions ensuring compliance with corporate policies, rules, and regulations at all levels. Based on the close relationships built with internal and external stakeholders, the incumbent will assist the office to regularly communicate and support implementation of best practices in financial management and accountability tasks. The position will assist the office in budget and expenditure analysis, programme delivery monitoring, operational performance tracking, and management reporting to facilitate evidence-based planning, decision-making, and effective implementation of the country programme. The position will also support management decision-making through analysis of programme performance, operational trends, and compliance risks.

You would be responsible for:

Operational effectiveness, programme compliance, risk management, and quality assurance:

  • Support quality assurance reviews of compliance processes, including follow-up on audit recommendations, management responses and internal oversight findings.
  • Support in ERM related activities for the country office.
  • Support the development and implementation of oversight mechanisms for Country Office operations.
  • Support the assessment of the Internal Control Framework and assist in identifying internal control weaknesses, gaps, inefficiencies and overlaps.
  • Support the identification of deviations from established rules and regulations and bring them to the attention of the International Operations Manager for appropriate follow-up.
  • Support analysis of programme delivery, expenditure trends, implementation rates, and operational performance and provide inputs to identify bottlenecks and possible corrective actions.
  • Support in preparing periodic compliance, assurance, risk management, and operational performance reports and dashboards for Country Office management to support decision-making and strategic oversight.

Support to Implementing Partners Oversight and HACT assurance plan:

  • Support in conducting periodic due diligence for vetting of IPs.
  • Support the assessment of implementing partner risks and contribute to the identification of appropriate mitigation measures under the guidance of the International Operations Manager.
  • Assist in checking accuracy and validity of signatories and bank accounts in the IP agreement, with particular attention to high-risk management areas, such as sub-contracting, procurement, cash management.
  • Assist in the implementation of the approved HACT Assurance Plan under the guidance of the International Operations Manager.
  • Support the implementation of quarterly financial monitoring, in close coordination with relevant Programme Units and Area Offices and assist in validating the completion of programme activities as reported by IPs.
  • Support conduct spot checks and compliance reviews of IPs to ensure that financial, procurement and HR processes are in line with IPs established procedures and the requirements of HACT.
  • Support the review of audit reports and assist in documenting agreed follow-up actions in coordination with programme staff, implementing partners and auditors.
  • Support the review of findings from assessments, monitoring, verification, spot checks and audits, and assist in tracking follow-up actions and implementation of agreed mitigation measures.
  • Support in the regular updating of the United Nations Programme Portal (UNPP) platform by taking care of uploading all required documents and ensuring the quality of the information within it.

Programme Performance Monitoring and Financial Oversight:

  • Support to ensure alignment between approved cash limits and work plan budgets. Provide inputs from a finance and compliance perspective, supporting the accurate allocation of direct and indirect costs, and ensuring that all budgeted items reflect eligible expenditures in line with UNFPA financial guidelines.
  • Support the programme and finance team on timely and accurate review and clearance of work plans and eFace reports, ensuring compliance with UNFPA guidelines.
  • Support the finance team in the OFA reconciliation process avoiding negative OFAs at the end of the year.
  • Contributes to reviews, annual planning exercises, audits, and oversight processes through data analysis and operational reporting.
  • Support the development and maintenance of operational dashboards and tracking tools to strengthen accountability, transparency, and results-based management.

Performing Additional Duties as Assigned:

  • Carry out additional administrative and support tasks as required by UNFPA leadership.
  • Collaborates with team members, programme partners, and sub-grantees to ensure safe implementation of programmes at the community level applying Do No Harm approach.

Qualifications and Experience:

Education:

  • Advanced university degree in Finance/Accounting, Business, or Public Administration or a related field.

Knowledge and Experience:

  • Professional experience in finance or audit, or other directly related fields is advantageous.
  • Experience in the usage of computers and office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc) and advanced knowledge of spreadsheet and database packages, experience in handling web-based management systems and ERP financials.
  • Prior experience in working with ERP systems (preferably Oracle based) is an advantage.
  • Previous experience in the UN and knowledge of UN internal control, risk management and implementing partner procedures is advantageous.
  • Excellent organizational skills, attention to detail, precision, and accuracy.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Should also possess the ability to formulate business requirements into logical system specifications.
  • Must be able to work in harmony across teams, both internally and externally.

Languages: Fluency in oral and written English and national language of the duty station.

Required Competencies:

Values:

  • Exemplifying integrity,
  • Demonstrating commitment to UNFPA and the UN system,
  • Embracing cultural diversity,
  • Embracing change.

Core Competencies:

  • Achieving results,
  • Being accountable,
  • Developing and applying professional expertise/business acumen,
  • Thinking analytically and strategically,
  • Working in teams/managing ourselves and our relationships,
  • Communicating for impact.

Functional Competencies:

  • Business acumen,
  • Implementing management systems,
  • Innovation and marketing of new approaches,
  • Client orientation,
  • Organizational awareness.

Compensation and Benefits:

This position offers an attractive remuneration package including a competitive net salary plus health insurance and other benefits as applicable.

UNFPA Work Environment:

UNFPA provides a work environment that reflects the values of gender equality, diversity, integrity and healthy work-life balance. We are committed to ensuring gender parity in the organization and therefore encourage women to apply. Individuals from the LGBTQIA+ community, minority ethnic groups, indigenous populations, persons with disabilities, and other underrepresented groups are highly encouraged to apply. Reasonable accommodation may be provided to applicants with disabilities upon request, to support their participation in the recruitment process. UNFPA promotes equal opportunities in terms of appointment, training, compensation and selection for all regardless of personal characteristics and dimensions of diversity. Diversity, Equity and Inclusion is at the heart of UNFPA’s workforce – click here to learn more.

Disclaimer:

Selection and appointment may be subject to background and reference checks, medical clearance, visa issuance and other administrative requirements.

UNFPA does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process and does not concern itself with information on applicants’ bank accounts.

Applicants for positions in the international Professional and higher categories, who hold permanent resident status in a country other than their country of nationality, may be required to renounce such status upon their appointment.

  • Fixed Term, Full Time Role based in Kathmandu, Nepal.

ABOUT THE FRED HOLLOWS FOUNDATION

The Fred Hollows Foundation is an international development organisation working to prevent blindness and restore sight. We continue to carry on the legacy of Professor Fred Hollows, who believed every person had the right to quality eye care, no matter where they live. The Foundation is known around the world as an organisation that works with purpose and determination. With a reputation for excellence, we are well known for making change happen.

The Foundation has grown to work in more than 25+ countries throughout Africa, South Asia, Southeast Asia, the Middle East and the Pacific, as well as Australia. The Foundation has restored sight to more than 3 million people worldwide. We have an ambitious five-year strategic plan that aims to take us even closer to realising our vision of a world in which no person is needlessly blind, or vision impaired and Indigenous Australians exercise their right to sight and good health. To find out more about our work, please visit our website https://www.hollows.org

THE OPPORTUNITY

The Program Coordinator (PC) is accountable for the coordination, implementation, and monitoring of FHF Nepal project activities, working closely with the Nepal Eye Program – Tilganga Institute of Ophthalmology (TIO), regional partner hospitals, government stakeholders, and all other relevant stakeholders.

The PC will also support relevant components of the broader FHF Nepal project, ensuring alignment, collaboration, and evidence generation across multisectoral platforms. Based in Kathmandu, the role involves close coordination with TIO and government stakeholders, and may require domestic or international travel when needed.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Key areas of accountability include:

  • Coordinate day-to-day implementation of the FHF Nepal project, ensuring alignment with Nepal country strategy, project goals, and FHF values.
  • Develop project workplans and ensure timely, high-quality delivery of all project activities.
  • Support integration of eye health into the primary health system, in line with Nepal’s Government Eye Health Strategy.
  • Serve as the primary focal point for TIO, regional partner hospitals, government stakeholders, and other stakeholders.
  • Coordinate and maintain a multi-stakeholder steering committee, facilitating regular meetings and effective collaboration across partners.
  • Organise and support training activities with TIO, including training for a range of relevant participants.
  • Contribute to effective project implementation through regular, high-quality planning, implementation, monitoring, reporting, and evaluation.

BACKGROUND

Established in 1992, ANSAB is a non-profit, non-governmental organization committed to biodiversity conservation and livelihood improvement in Nepal. It places community empowerment and economic incentives at the heart of its approach and generates knowledge and results through applied research and studies to implement innovative solutions. ANSAB has been consistently evolving, consolidating, institutionalizing and advancing the approaches and strategies for the promotion of community-based enterprises and value chains, natural resources management and biodiversity conservation, enabling policy environment and multi-stakeholders.

ANSAB is urgently seeking to recruit a qualified, dynamic, and results-oriented individual for the position of Forest Officer under a project entitled “Scaling Conservation of Himalayan Plants and Fungi through Sustainable Trade”.

SCOPE OF WORK

The forest officer, based in Darchula, will be responsible for the efficient and timely execution of project activities at Darchula and Bajhang districts. Under the overall supervision of Senior Manager- Biodiversity and with day-to-day reporting to Field Program Coordinator, the Forest Officer will oversee and coordinate project activities in these two districts. QUALIFICATION AND SKILLS

  • M.Sc. in Forestry, or M.Sc. in Natural Resource Management with a B.Sc. in Forestry, and at least one year of experience working in Himalayan districts;

  • Excellent interpersonal and written communication skills in English and Nepali;

UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence.

At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling.

UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package.

Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF.

For every child, the right to Education

How can you make a difference?

UNICEF Nepal’s Education Section works with the Government of Nepal and development partners to improve access, equity, quality, governance and resilience in school education. The School Education Sector Plan (SESP) 2022-2032 is entering a decisive transition: a realistic and costed second five-year programme for 2027-2032 and a successor Joint Financing Arrangement must be developed while foundational learning, digitalization, inclusive education and federal service delivery are translated into practical sector arrangements. From August 2026, UNICEF serves as the Development Partner focal point, with the Embassy of Finland as co-focal point, creating a time-bound need for strong coordination, analysis, representation and follow-up. The role will also help inform the Local Education Development Partner Group of the work done through the Nepal Education Cluster in terms of the response and early-recovery work following the August 2026 floods.

Join UNICEF Nepal’s Education Section to support the country’s long-standing sector-wide approach at a decisive transition. You will help UNICEF in undertaking its Development Partner focal-point responsibilities, coordinate closely with the Ministry of Education and Sports and the Embassy of Finland, and connect sector dialogue with UNICEF programme and field evidence.

Your key functions and accountabilities will cover:

  • UNICEF core-team and focal-point coordination. Support planning, preparation and follow-up for UNICEF’s engagement with Government, Joint Financing Partners, LEDPG/LEG members and other stakeholders; maintain day-to-day coordination with MoES DACS and the Embassy of Finland; and prepare calendars, agendas, briefs, speaking points, meeting records, decision logs and action trackers.
  • Support to the second SESP programme (2027-2032). Coordinate UNICEF inputs to the Government-led roadmap, evidence review, consultations, drafting and decision calendar; promote foundational learning; facilitate meaningful federal, provincial and local consultation; and synthesize specialist inputs.
  • Support to the successor Joint Financing Arrangement. Organize UNICEF and partner contributions to the review and successor dialogue, improve the visibility of partner financing, coordinate specialist advice and maintain consultation records, comment matrices and action trackers.
  • Subnational participation and accountability. Help provincial education plans, Local Education Plans, budgets, implementation monitoring and frontline learning evidence inform federal dialogue, joint reviews and SESP II design.
  • Programme management, communication and risk management. Maintain an agreed workplan and milestones, provide decision-oriented analysis, identify and escalate risks, coordinate with UNICEF programme and operations colleagues and field offices, and undertake authorized official travel.
  • Education response and early recovery. Support regular updates to the LEDPG and coordination of response and early-recovery initiatives so that evidence and lessons from flood-affected areas inform joint sector reviews and planning.
  • If you would like to know more about this position, please review the complete Job Description here: Download File JD_Education Officer (Sector Coordination), NOB, TA, Kathmandu, Nepal #00138273.pdf

To qualify as an advocate for every child you will have…

Minimum requirements:

Education: University degree (Bachelor’s) in education, public policy or administration, economics, development studies, social sciences or another relevant field is required.

Work Experience: Minimum two years of relevant professional experience in education programme planning, management, partnerships, coordination, policy support or a related area is required. Experience working with Government institutions and/or development partners and supporting multi-stakeholder processes, experience organizing high level external meetings or consultations, synthesizing evidence and diverse inputs, and preparing clear briefs, records or action trackers is required. Experience managing several priorities and deadlines through collaborative work with different stakeholders is a requirement.

Technical skills required:

  • Good understanding of Nepal’s school education sector and federal governance context, including the respective roles of federal, provincial and local institutions.
  • Ability to review policy, program, financing and implementation information and translate it into concise options, briefs and follow-up actions appropriate to the level of the post.
  • Strong coordination, facilitation, relationship-management and teamwork skills, with sound judgment about institutional roles, clearances and escalation.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint and familiarity with collaborative document, virtual-meeting and knowledge-management tools.

Language Requirements: English and Nepali – Proficient/Fluent level is required.

Desirables:

  • Familiarity with Nepal’s SESP, SWAp, JFA, JRM/BRM, LEDPG/JFP processes, IEMIS or Local Education Plans will be an asset.
  • Exposure to foundational learning, inclusive education, digital education, public financing, results-based financing, partner-financing mapping or subnational service delivery is deired.
  •  Prior experience with UNICEF/UN or an international development institution is an asset.
  •  Knowledge of another official UN language is an asset.

For every Child, you demonstrate…

UNICEF’s Core Values of Care, Respect, Integrity, Trust and Accountability and Sustainability (CRITAS) underpin everything we do and how we do it. Get acquainted with Our Values Charter: UNICEF Values

UNICEF competencies required for this post are…

(1) Builds and maintains partnerships

The Senior Coordinator, Child Protection will lead the implementation, coordination, monitoring, and technical oversight of child protection interventions within the flood response programs. The position will ensure that child protection risks are identified, monitored, and addressed through quality programming, coordination with relevant stakeholders, and integration across the wider humanitarian response. The role will carry out child protection analysis, information management, and reporting while ensuring adherence to safeguarding, child rights, and humanitarian standards.

Position: Inclusive Humanitarian Lead
Employment type: Full-time: fixed-term contract of twelve months
Duty station: NAB Central Office, Sukedhara, Kathmandu, with frequent travel to Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading
Reports to: Director, Nepal Association of the Blind
Salary: NPR 100,000 per month (gross)
Apply before: 15th September 2026

Background

Nepal Association of the Blind (NAB) is the national umbrella organization of blind and partially sighted people in Nepal. NAB works to promote the rights, inclusion, and empowerment of people with visual impairments through advocacy, capacity building, and service delivery. The Nepal Association of the Blind (NAB), with support from the Norwegian Association of Blind and Partially Sighted (NABP), is implementing Restoring Independence, a twelve-month disability-inclusive response to the August 2026 Bhote Koshi–Trishuli floods in Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading. NAB invites applications from qualified Nepali citizens for the following position.

Major Responsibilities

  • Lead the planning, implementation, budgeting and quality assurance of the project, and supervise the project team.
  • Lead the accessible needs assessment, ensure disability-disaggregated data using the Washington Group Questions, and produce the assessment report for NDRRMA and NABP.
  • Oversee accessible referral, individual need-based support and community-based psychosocial counselling for persons with disabilities.
  • Represent NAB with NDRRMA, local governments, NFDN, local OPDs and the humanitarian clusters, and advocate for disability-inclusive help desks and an accessible disaster response hotline.
  • Lead orientation on disability-inclusive disaster risk reduction, the DIDRR manual and accessible IEC materials.
  • Ensure compliance with NAB’s safeguarding and PSEAH policies, and prepare timely narrative and financial reports.

Required Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in social sciences, development studies, disaster risk management, public health, social work or a related field. A Bachelor’s degree with strong additional experience may be considered.
  • At least five years’ experience in humanitarian response, disaster risk reduction or development programming in Nepal, including two years in a leadership or project management role.
  • Demonstrated experience of disability inclusion, or of working with or within organizations of persons with disabilities.
  • Working knowledge of the UNCRPD, the Act Relating to Rights of Persons with Disabilities 2074, the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act 2074, and the IASC Guidelines on Inclusion of Persons with Disabilities in Humanitarian Action.
  • Excellent written and spoken Nepali and English, strong report writing and team management skills, and computer proficiency.
  • Willingness to travel and work in flood-affected areas under difficult conditions.
  • A valid driving license for a two-wheeler or four-wheeler will be an advantage/preference, given the frequent travel to flood-affected areas.

The UN Secretary-General launched on 1 January 2019 a bold and new global reform which repositioned the UN Development System to deliver more effectively and efficiently the achievement of the 2030 Agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals. As part of this reform, UN Resident Coordinator Offices (UN RCO), under the leadership of an empowered and independent UN Resident Coordinator, support countries in the achievement of their development priorities and the attainment of the SDGs. The position is located in the United Nations Resident Coordination Office (RCO) in Kathmandu, Nepal. Under the direct supervision of the Head of Office and guidance of the RC and in full confidentiality, the Executive Assistant ensures effective and efficient functioning of the RC Front-Office, overall management of the RC’s schedule and logistical requirements, maintenance of protocol procedures, management of information flow, and follow-up on deadlines and commitments made.

Responsibilities

Within delegated authority, the Executive Assistant will be responsible for the following duties:

1. ENSURE EFFECTIVE AND EFFICIENT FUNCTIONING OF THE RC FRONT OFFICE FOCUSING ON ACHIEVEMENT OF THE FOLLOWING RESULTS:

  •  Maintain the Resident Coordinator’s calendar and representation schedule, arrange appointments and meetings of the RC, provide protocol coverage, ensure logistical details of RC participation in events, and act as an interpreter and/or taking minutes of meetings when required.
  •  Coordinate high-quality briefing materials for the RC for appointments, meetings, events, and missions and ensure that all correspondence and documents submitted to the RC are according to UN norms and standards including directives, coordinate comments on behalf of RC for signature and action/follow-up when required.
  •  Draft key correspondence, including notes to files, minutes of meetings and Note Verbales, and provide translation for official correspondence.
  • Prioritize tasks, meeting deadlines, and managing executive schedules effectively.
  • Anticipate issues and resolve them before they affect the executive’s work.
  • Manage RC travel and missions, prepare travel requests, ensure flight bookings and provision of logistics information, and follow up on trip reports and travel claims.
  • Maintain contact lists of high-level partners, UN Agencies, and Diplomatic Corps.
  •  Assist in organizing official events: travel (booking flights, request for security clearance, arrangements at airport, etc.) for local and high-level visitors as required.
  •  In collaboration with the RCO team, prepare and maintain checklists and templates for relevant processes (high level visits, meetings preparation etc).
  •  Provide all similar services and support to RC a.i.
  •  Remain effective in fast-changing environments and shifting priorities.
  •  Act as a trusted partner who anticipates needs and helps executives stay focused on priorities.

2. ENSURE PROVISION OF EFFECTIVE COMMUNICATIONS SUPPORT TO THE OFFICE FOCUSING ON THE ACHIEVEMENT OF THE FOLLOWING RESULTS:

  • Demonstrated ability to communicate clearly, professionally, and effectively, both orally and in writing, with internal and external stakeholders at all levels.
  • Handle sensitive information with professionalism and trustworthiness.
  • Have proven track record of strong working relationships with government and other external partners including ability to build strong relationships with colleagues, especially decision makers.
  • Maintain the filing system (in TEAMS/Sharepoint) ensuring safekeeping of confidential materials. Use of automated filing system.
  •  Screen RC incoming calls and correspondence.
  • Demonstrate ability to use AI, Strong skills in Microsoft 365, Teams, Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, and collaboration tools.
  • Coordinate the activities of the RC driver.
  •  Support organize and communicate on the various coordination meetings, including UNCT Meetings.
  • Participate in the organization of official UN Days, public events, joint UN events and provide secretariat and administrative support to the UNCT
  • Follow up on deadlines, commitments made, actions taken and coordination of collection and submission of the reports to RC.

3. HUMAN RESOURCES MANAGEMENT:

  • Provide support to the RC in matters such as documentation, visas, travel arrangements, house and school search, etc.

4. OFFICE ADMINISTRATION:

  • Act as an alternate to the RCO Administrative Assistant when required to support RCO in day to-day administrative tasks as required, including contract administration, budget and finance, and human resource management.
  •  Assists with the collection and analysis of data as well as preparation of data presentations and reports for information sharing, responding to queries, knowledge management, planning and decision making.
  •  Assists with visualizations and updating information material such as web pages or brochures.
  •  Ensures that requirements and background information used for data analysis are documented.
  • Performs other relevant duties as assigned.

Competencies

Professionalism:

Ability to perform a broad range of administrative functions, e.g., budget/work programme, human resources, database management, etc.

Ability to apply knowledge of various United Nations administrative, financial and human resources rules and regulations in work situations.
Ability to apply sustainable development theories, concepts and approaches.
Ability to conduct independent research and analysis on sustainable development topics, determine suitability, validity and accuracy of data provided by different sources.
Shows skill in developing sources for data collection.
Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations; commitment to implementing the goal of gender equality by ensuring the equal participation and full involvement of women and men in all aspects of work.

Communication: Speaks and writes clearly and effectively; listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately; asks questions to clarify, and exhibits interest in having two-way communication; tailors language, tone, style and format to match audience; demonstrates openness In sharing information and keeping people informed.

Teamwork: Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others’ ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda; supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings.

Education

  • Completion of a High school diploma or equivalent is required. Bachelors or advanced university degree in business administration, office management, communication or related fields would be an advantage.

Work Experience

  • A minimum of seven (7) years of experience in administrative support, coordination, logistics or front office functions is required.
  • The minimum years of relevant experience is reduced by two (2) years for candidates who possess a first level University degree.
  • Demonstrated experience in supporting senior officials or executive offices, including protocol arrangements is desirable.
  • Demonstrated experience in organizing meetings, missions and high-level events, including coordination with internal and external stakeholders is desirable.
  • Work experience with the United Nations, international organization, diplomatic mission or government institution is desirable.
  • One(1) year or more of experience in data analytics or related area is desirable.
